title: Approvals and the Waitlist
summary: How join requests work on rides where the organizer approves riders, and how the waitlist fills open spots on a full ride.

Organizers can choose to approve each rider on a public ride, and can cap how many riders or vehicles come along. Here's what happens on both sides.

## Rides That Need Approval

When creating a public ride, the organizer picks **I Approve Riders** under **Joining**. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).

### If You're Asking to Join

1. Open the ride page.
2. Tap **Request to Join**.

The page shows "Your request is waiting for the organizer." You get a notification when you're approved. Until then you don't see the exact meeting point or the group.

This is the same whether you found the ride on **Find** or opened it with its link, QR code or invite code. Only riders the organizer invited through a riding group skip approval. See [Invite Riders](/help/invite-riders).

### If You're the Organizer

You get a notification when someone asks to join. Then:

1. Open the ride page. The **Riders** section shows a red count of requests waiting.
2. Tap **Riders**.
3. Under **Waiting for You**, tap **Approve** or **Decline** next to each rider.

If you set **Max Riders** or **Max Vehicles** and the ride is already full, a rider you approve goes on the waitlist instead. They move up automatically when a spot opens.

## The Waitlist

If the organizer set **Max Riders** or **Max Vehicles** and the ride is full, new riders go on the waitlist. That includes riders the organizer approves and riders invited through a riding group. The page shows "You're on the waitlist. You'll move up automatically if a spot opens."

When a rider leaves, riders on the waitlist move up in the order they joined, as long as they fit. You get a notification when you have a spot.

The **Spots** line on the ride page shows how full the ride is, like "8 of 10 vehicles". Riders on the ride can see how many are on the waitlist under the **Going** list.

## Leaving the Waitlist or a Request

Open the ride page and tap **Leave Ride**, or swipe left on the ride on the **Rides** tab and tap **Leave**.

:::note
If the ride is cancelled, riders who asked to join or are on the waitlist get a notification and an email too.
:::

articles.summary: Choose how often your phone sends your location while you share, to make the battery last longer on long days.
articles.text:
---
title: Use Battery Saver
summary: Choose how often your phone sends your location while you share, to make the battery last longer on long days.
category: safety-privacy
order: 15
release: "1.0.1"
updated: 2026-10-15
sources:
  - app/src/app/battery.tsx
  - app/src/core/battery.ts
  - app/src/lib/battery.ts
  - app/src/lib/location.ts
related: [location-sharing, ride-mode, troubleshooting]
keywords: [battery, battery saver, battery life, power, gps, update rate, accuracy, low power, drain]
---

Sharing your location keeps the GPS on and sends your position to your group. Battery Saver lets you trade how often your group sees you move for a longer-lasting battery. It starts on **Best Accuracy**, which is what we recommend whenever you can charge your phone.

## The Three Settings

| Setting | Your dot updates about every | What your group notices |
|---|---|---|
| **Best Accuracy** (Recommended) | 15 seconds or 25 m (80 ft) | Your dot follows you closely. Best for following the leader and for finding someone who stopped. |
| **Balanced** | 30 seconds or 75 m (250 ft) | Your dot can trail up to 30 seconds behind you. |
| **Max Battery Saver** | 45 seconds or 200 m (650 ft) | Your dot can trail up to 45 seconds behind you and be off by up to about 100 m (330 ft). For multi-day trips with no way to charge. |

On every setting, a phone that is parked still checks in often enough that your group sees you as live, not as **No Signal**. Taps like **Need Help** and **EMERGENCY** always send right away.

Battery Saver also slows Ride Mode's own work on your phone: your blue dot on the route moves in bigger steps, and the backup check for other riders runs less often. Other riders still appear the moment their phones send.

## Change the Setting

1. Go to the **You** tab and tap **Battery Saver**. You can also tap **Change** next to **Battery Saver** at the bottom of **Share My Location**.
2. Tap the setting you want.
3. If you picked **Balanced** or **Max Battery Saver**, the app tells you what your group loses and asks you to confirm. Tap **Use Balanced** or **Use Max Battery Saver**, or **Keep Current** to leave it.

The change takes effect right away, even in the middle of a share. While you're on Balanced or Max Battery Saver, the sharing banner in Ride Mode shows the setting's name, and **Switch Back to Best Accuracy** is at the top of the Battery Saver screen.

:::note
Battery Saver is set on each phone or tablet separately, and other riders aren't told which setting you picked.
:::

## Other Ways to Save Battery

- Download an [offline map](/help/offline-maps) before you lose service, so the phone isn't searching for map tiles.
- Stop sharing when you don't need to. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).
- Keep the phone on a charger or a 12V outlet on long rides.

Checking in tells the organizer and the rest of the group that you're at the meeting spot and ready to ride.

## Check In

1. Open the ride page.
2. Tap **I'm Here and Ready**.

The button changes to "Checked in at" and the time you tapped it.

You can check in once you've joined the ride, until the ride ends. Checking in doesn't use your location. It does need a connection, so if the trailhead has no signal, check in before you lose it.

## See Who's Here

On the ride page, tap **Riders**. Riders who checked in show **Here** under their name in the **Going** list. Organizers use this to see who's made it before starting Ride Mode.

:::note
Once you've checked in, you can't undo it.
:::

:::tip
Need help getting to the meeting spot? Directions are on the ride page once you've joined. See [Directions](/help/directions).
:::

---

Questions, problems or ideas for OnMyLead go straight to the team at RUS Offroad. A real person reads every message.

:::warning
OnMyLead is not an emergency service. In an emergency, call 911 or your local emergency number first.
:::

## Send a Message From the App

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Help**, tap **Contact Us**.
3. Under **What's It About?**, pick a topic:
   - **Something Isn't Working**
   - **Feature Request**
   - **Billing and Pro**
   - **Account and Sign-In**
   - **Safety or a Rider**
   - **General Feedback**
   - **Something Else**
4. Check **Your Name** (optional) and **Your Email**. If you're signed in, they're filled in for you.
5. Write **Your Message**. The hint under the box suggests what to include for your topic.
6. Tap **Send Message**.

You'll see **Message Sent**. We reply to the email you gave, usually within a day.

:::release 1.0.1
## Report a Bug

If something in the app isn't working, tell us with a screenshot so we can fix it fast.

1. Take a screenshot of the problem:
   - **iPhone**: press the side button and volume up together.
   - **iPad**: press the top button and a volume button together.
   - **Android phone or tablet**: press the power and volume down buttons together.
2. Go to the **You** tab. Under **Help**, tap **Report a Bug**. The form opens with **Something Isn't Working** already picked.
3. Tap **Add a Screenshot** and pick your screenshot. Tap **Change Screenshot** or **Remove** if you picked the wrong one.
4. Write what you tapped, what happened and what you expected, then tap **Send Message**.

Your report also includes your phone model, your OnMyLead version, the screen you were on before you opened the form, and a short log of what the app just did (the screens you opened, errors and requests that failed). The log never includes your location, your messages or anything you typed, and it's kept only in memory: it's gone when you close the app.

On onmylead.com/contact, pick **Something Isn't Working** to add a screenshot the same way. Your browser goes with the report instead of a phone model.
:::

## Send a Message From the Website

Go to onmylead.com/contact. The same form works there, and you don't need to sign in.

## Email Us

You can also email support@rusoffroad.com.

## Tips for a Quick Answer

- **Something Isn't Working**: tell us what you tapped, what happened and what you expected. The ride name helps if it's about a ride.
- **Billing and Pro**: purchases are billed by Apple, and refunds go through reportaproblem.apple.com. We're still glad to help.

On Android, the hint says purchases are billed by Google Play, with refunds through your Google Play order history.
- **Account and Sign-In**: if you sign in with a different email than the one on the form, tell us which.
- **Safety or a Rider**: to report a rider, you can also press and hold their message in a ride. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

## Help and Support Page

Under **Help** on the **You** tab, **Help and Support** has short answers to common questions about joining rides, location and battery, Pro, blocking and deleting your account.

In the Android app, those answers give the Android steps where they differ, such as allowing location **While Using the App**.

You can plan a ride on the big screen at onmylead.com. It's the same ride as one made in the app: the ride, its route and its stops show up in the OnMyLead app on your phone or tablet as soon as you save. Ride Mode and live tracking stay in the app.

![Drawing a route on onmylead.com](/help/img/web-route.webp)

## Create a Ride on the Web

1. Go to onmylead.com and click **Create a Ride on the Web**.
2. Sign in with your OnMyLead account if you aren't already. You go straight to Create a Ride after signing in.
3. Pick **Public** or **Private** under **What Kind of Ride?**
4. Fill in the **Ride Name**, the day under **When**, and the **Meet At** time. Click **Calendar** to pick any day from today up to a year out.
5. Set the **Meeting Point**: click the satellite map to drop the pin, then drag the pin to fine-tune it. You can also search a place, use your location, or type coordinates, and the pin moves there.
6. Under **The Route**, pick **Mapped** or **Freeride**.
7. Fill in anything else you want, then click **Create Public Ride** or **Create Private Ride**.

The rest of the form works the same as in the app. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride) for every option.

## Draw the Route on the Web

If you picked **Mapped**, the route builder opens after you create the ride. Click along the trail and the route follows it. Drawing a route is free. Importing a GPX file is a Pro feature. See [Build a Route](/help/route-builder) and [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

You can also add numbered planned stops for fuel, lunch or camp. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

## Share It

After saving, your ride page shows the invite code, a QR code and share buttons, the same as in the app. See [Invite Riders](/help/invite-riders).

:::note
Free accounts create one ride each month, whether on the website or in the app. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
:::

:::tip
When someone opens a ride link on a computer, the page shows the ride's QR code. They can scan it with their phone's camera to open the ride on their phone.
:::

:::note
Stuck while planning? Click **Help** at the top of onmylead.com to open these guides.
:::

You lead. Create a ride, tell everyone where and when to meet, and OnMyLead gives you a link, a code and a QR code to share. Public rides show up for riders nearby. Private rides are only for the people you invite.

![The Create a Ride screen](/help/img/create.webp)

## Create Your Ride

1. On the **Rides** tab, tap **Create a Ride**.
2. Under **What Kind of Ride?**, tap **Public** (open to anyone, found by riders near you or in your state) or **Private** (only friends you invite by link, text or email).
3. Type a **Ride Name**.
4. Under **When**, pick the day (see [Pick the Day](#pick-the-day) below).
5. Type the time in **Meet At**, for example "8:00 am" or "2:30 pm".
6. Set the **Meeting Point**. You can search in **Search a Place or Address**, tap **Use My Current Location**, or paste **Coordinates** like "38.57, -109.55".
7. Add a **Place Name** if you like, such as "Gas station on Main St".
8. Under **The Route**, tap **Mapped** (you draw the route or import a GPX file next) or **Freeride** (no set route, everyone follows the leader).
9. Under **Who's Riding**, pick the **Vehicles Welcome**.
10. Tap **Create Public Ride** or **Create Private Ride**.

If you picked **Mapped**, the route builder opens right away so you can draw the trail. See [Build a Route](/help/route-builder). Once the ride is saved you land on its page, ready to invite riders.

:::tip
Only riders who have joined see the exact meeting spot. Public pages show the general area, within about a mile.
:::

## Pick the Day

:::until 1.0.1
Under **When**, tap **Today**, **Tomorrow** or any day in the next two weeks.
:::

:::release 1.0.1
Under **When**, tap **Today**, **Tomorrow**, **Sat** or **Sun** for the coming weekend. For any other day, tap **Calendar** and pick it from the month calendar. Use the arrows to go to another month. You can schedule a ride for any day from today up to a year out. The day you picked shows under **When**, with how far away it is, such as "In 8 Weeks".

On a tablet, the calendar sits in the same form, with bigger day buttons.
:::

## Public Ride Options

A public ride is listed in its state so riders can find it. The **State** fills in from the meeting point. If it's wrong (it can happen near a border), tap **Change State** and pick the right one.

Public rides also have a **Joining** choice:

- **Anyone Can Join**
- **I Approve Riders**

See [Approvals and the Waitlist](/help/approvals-and-waitlist) for how requests work. Private rides don't have this choice: anyone holding your invite link or code can join.

## Limit Who Can Come

Under **Who's Riding**, set **Max Vehicles**, **Max Riders** or both. Leave them empty for no limit. When the ride is full, new riders go on a waitlist. See [Approvals and the Waitlist](/help/approvals-and-waitlist).

## Invite a Riding Group

If you're in a riding group, an **Invite a Group** section shows up. Pick one or more groups under **Your Riding Groups**. Everyone in them gets a notification and sees the ride on their Rides tab, and they join with one tap. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups).

## Add More Details

Tap **Add Route, Difficulty and More** to fill in any of these:

- **Description**
- **Departure Time** and **Expected Finish** (used to check your ride against sunset, see [Ride Day and Weather](/help/ride-day-and-weather))
- **Destination**, which anyone who can see the ride sees, with directions in Apple Maps or Google Maps
- **Route Length (Miles)**, used to warn riders whose fuel range is too short (see [Fuel Range](/help/fuel-range))
- **Difficulty**: Easy, Moderate, Hard or Extreme
- **Experience**: Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced or Expert
- **What to Bring**, **Required Equipment** and **Fuel**
- **Instructions for Joined Riders**, which only riders on the ride see
- **Ride Bubble**: Standard, Tight Trail, Desert or Highway (see [Ride Bubble](/help/ride-bubble))

## After You Create It

Your ride page opens with a card that has the invite code, a QR code and buttons to share it. See [Invite Riders](/help/invite-riders). You're also the ride's organizer and leader. See [Organizer Controls](/help/organizer-controls).

## How Many Rides You Can Create

Free accounts create one ride each month. Joining rides is always free and unlimited. On Free, the top of the Create a Ride screen shows **Rides Created This Month** so you know where you stand. When you've used this month's free ride, the app tells you the date your next one opens (the first of the month, UTC). Creating more rides than that is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

:::note
A ride counts toward the month you create it, even if you later cancel or delete it. Copying a ride or using **Ride Again** also creates a new ride.
:::

Pro bought on Android through Google Play lifts the monthly limit the same way, on every device you sign in to.

You can delete your OnMyLead account yourself, right in the app. It happens straight away and can't be undone.

## Before You Delete

If you pay for OnMyLead Pro, cancel it with Apple too. Apple bills the subscription, so deleting your account doesn't stop it. See [Manage Your Subscription](/help/manage-subscription).

## Delete Your Account

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Scroll to the bottom and tap **Delete Account**.
3. Read the message, then tap **Delete Account** to confirm.

You're signed out and taken back to the start.

## What Gets Deleted

- Your account and profile.
- Rides you organize. They're removed for everyone on them.
- Your Garage, trips and riding groups.
- Your messages and location history.

This can't be undone. To ride with OnMyLead again later, you'd make a new account.

## If You See Deletion Requested

Sometimes the app shows **Deletion Requested** instead of signing you out. That means your request was sent and your account and its data will be deleted within 7 days. If you pay for Pro, cancel it in your Apple subscriptions so you aren't billed again.

## Need Help?

If the delete doesn't go through, [Contact Us](/help/contact-support) and pick **Account and Sign-In**.

OnMyLead hands you over to Apple Maps or Google Maps for turn-by-turn directions on the road. Off road, follow the leader and the route on the OnMyLead map.

On Android, directions open in Google Maps, since Android phones and tablets don't have Apple Maps.

Only the place you want to go is sent to the maps app, nothing about you.

## Get Directions to the Meeting Point

1. Open the ride from the **Rides** tab.
2. On the **Details** section, find the **Directions** card.
3. Tap a row:
   - **Meeting Point:** the exact meeting spot.
   - **Along the Route:** follows the ride's route through stops on the way, ending at the end of the route.
   - **Destination:** the ride's destination, if the organizer added one.
4. Pick **Apple Maps** or **Google Maps**, unless you've already chosen one (below).

The **Directions** card shows while the ride is scheduled or live. **Meeting Point** and **Along the Route** only show for riders who have joined the ride, because the exact meeting spot and the route are private to them. See [Privacy](/help/privacy).

## Get Directions in Ride Mode

1. In Ride Mode, tap **Directions** just above the bottom panel, on the left.
2. Tap a row:
   - **Regroup Point:** where the leader asked everyone to meet up, when one is set.
   - **Meeting Point**
   - **Continue Along the Route:** picks up from where you are on the route.
   - **Destination**
3. Pick your maps app, if asked.

You can also get directions from other places in Ride Mode:

- Tap the yellow **Regroup point set. Tap to navigate** banner.
- Tap **Navigate** on a rider's alert card.
- Open the **Riders** list and tap **Navigate**, or **Go to Last Seen** for a rider whose position is old.
- Tap a waypoint on the map. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

:::note
Directions along the route pass through up to 8 stops picked from the route, and the maps app keeps to roads it knows between them. Off-road parts of the route may differ, so follow the OnMyLead map there.
:::

## Choose Your Maps App

1. Tap the **You** tab.
2. Under **Settings**, tap **Directions**.
3. Pick **Ask Each Time**, **Apple Maps** or **Google Maps**.
4. Tap **Done**.

Every **Navigate** and **Directions** button in the app uses this choice. With **Ask Each Time**, the app asks which one to open every time.

:::tip
Google Maps opens in its app if you have it installed, and in your browser if you don't.
:::

Plans change. As the organizer you can update the route and stops, cancel the ride so everyone knows it's off, or delete it entirely.

## What You Can Change

On your ride page, you can change:

- **The route.** Open the **Map** section and tap **Edit Route** (or **Build the Route** if there isn't one yet, or **Map a Route Anyway** on a freeride). See [Build a Route](/help/route-builder).
- **Planned stops.** In the **Map** section, tap **Add a Planned Stop**. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).
- **Who leads and who rides at the rear.** See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).

:::note
The ride's name, day, meeting time and meeting point can't be changed after the ride is created. To move a ride, tap **Copy This Ride** on its page to start a new one with the same details and route, pick the new day, then cancel the old one. The copy counts as a new ride toward your monthly allowance on Free.
:::

## Cancel a Ride

Cancel when the ride is off but you want everyone to see that it was called off. The ride stays in their list as Cancelled.

1. Open the ride page.
2. In the **You're Organizing** card on **Details**, tap **Cancel Ride**.
3. Read the message. It tells you how many riders will hear about it.
4. Tap **Cancel Ride** to confirm, or **Keep Ride** to go back.

Everyone who joined, asked to join or is on the waitlist gets a notification and an email saying the ride is cancelled. Cancelling can't be undone.

You can cancel a ride that hasn't started yet or one that's live. A ride that has already ended can't be cancelled.

## Delete a Ride

Delete removes the ride for everyone, along with its chat and route. Only the ride's organizer can delete it.

1. Open the ride page.
2. In the **You're Organizing** card, tap **Delete Ride**.
3. Tap **Delete Ride** to confirm.

If the ride hadn't ended yet, everyone on it gets a notification and an email saying it's cancelled. Deleting can't be undone.

:::tip
You can also delete a ride from the **Rides** tab. Swipe left on the ride under **Your Rides** or **Past Rides** and tap **Delete**.
:::

## Cancel or Delete: Which One?

- **Cancel** keeps the ride in everyone's list, marked Cancelled.
- **Delete** removes it, its chat and its route for everyone.

Either way, riders on an upcoming ride are told it's off.

:::note
Cancelling or deleting doesn't give back a ride on a Free account. A ride counts toward the month you created it. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
:::

:::warning
OnMyLead is not an emergency service. It does not contact 911, search and rescue, or anyone outside your ride. If anyone is hurt, call 911 or your local emergency number first.
:::

OnMyLead helps your group keep track of each other. Phones lose signal, batteries die, and positions can be late or wrong, so use it alongside your own plan, not instead of one.

Everything on this page is free on every plan. None of it needs Pro.

## What EMERGENCY Does

The **EMERGENCY** button in Ride Mode alerts everyone on your ride at once.

1. In Ride Mode, tap **EMERGENCY**. It stays on screen even when the bottom panel is folded.
2. Read the **Emergency** screen. If you're sharing your location, it shows your coordinates in large type, so you can read them out on a call.
3. Press and hold **Alert My Group** until it sends. A quick tap won't send it.
4. If anyone is hurt, tap **Call 911** to open your phone's dialer.

Tap **Cancel** to close the screen without sending anything.

When the alert goes out:

- Every rider on the ride gets a notification, "EMERGENCY: your name needs help now", with "Tap to see where they are."
- It shows in red on their Ride Mode screen. If you're sharing your location, they see you on the map and can tap **Navigate** to get directions to you.
- Help and EMERGENCY notifications are always on for every rider, even in quiet hours, and they come through even from a rider someone has blocked.

You see a card showing whose phones have the alert. If you sent it by mistake, tap **Cancel** on the card and the group is told to ignore it. See [Send a Status or Quick Reply](/help/status-buttons).

## What EMERGENCY Doesn't Do

- It doesn't call or text 911, emergency services, or anyone else.
- It doesn't reach anyone who isn't on the ride.
- It can't send without a connection. With no service, the alert waits on your phone and sends by itself when you get signal. Riders also need service to receive it.

## Need Help

**Need Help** is for when you need the group but it isn't an emergency. It sends with one tap, shows in red for the group, and notifies everyone on the ride the same way, including during quiet hours.

When things are sorted, tap **Resolved, I'm OK** so the group knows.

## Ride Safer

- **Call 911 first** in an emergency, then alert your group.
- **Share your location for the whole ride**, so Ride Bubble and the group can see you, and so riders can find you if you call for help. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).
- **Send a family link** to someone at home, and tell them when you expect to be back. See [Share a Family Link](/help/family-link).
- **Download the ride's map** before you lose signal. The map keeps working offline, but positions only update with a connection. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).
- **Allow notifications** so you hear when someone needs help. See [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).
- **Allow location Always**, so your group can see you with your phone locked.

On Android, allow location **While Using the App**: the **Sharing Your Location** notification keeps your group seeing you with the phone locked. **Need Help** and **EMERGENCY** arrive in the **Rider Alerts** notification category, which Android shows at the highest priority.
- **Never type or read the screen while driving or riding.** Pull over first. Ride Mode is built for one-tap use when you're stopped.
- **Carry what you need to get yourself home**, and ride within your skill and your machine's limits.

---

A family link is a web link you can text to someone at home. They open it in any web browser, with no app and no account, and see your last known location and when sharing ends. It's free on every plan.

## Send a Family Link

1. Tap the **You** tab.
2. Under **On the Trail**, tap **Share My Location**.
3. Turn on **Family Link**.
4. Under **For How Long**, pick how long to share. If you pick **Until I Turn It Off (Max 24 Hours)**, tap **Share** to confirm.
5. Your iPhone's share sheet opens with a message like "Follow my location until 5:30 PM" and the link. Pick Messages, or any app, and send it.

You can pick riders under **Who Can See You** at the same time, or send just the family link.

## What They See

The link opens a simple page with:

- Your ride name.
- **Last update:** when your phone last sent its location.
- **Sharing ends:** when the link stops working.
- **Open in Maps:** opens your last location in Google Maps.

The page checks for a new location every 30 seconds. If your phone hasn't sent a location yet, it says **No location received yet.**

:::warning
The page shows your last update, not a guaranteed live position. With no service on the trail, **Last update** stays at the last time your phone got through. Tell your family what time you expect to be back, and what to do if they don't hear from you.
:::

## Stop or Extend the Link

The family link lasts exactly as long as the share it belongs to.

1. Tap the **You** tab, then **Share My Location**.
2. Find the card that says **Includes a family link**.
3. Tap **Add 1 Hour** to keep it going, or **Stop** to end it now.

Once the share ends, the link shows **No Longer Shared** and **This location link has ended.** Your location can't be seen from it again.

:::note
Anyone who has the link can see your location until the share ends, so only send it to people you trust.
:::

## Is OnMyLead Free?

Yes. Free accounts create one ride each calendar month and can join as many rides as they like, and the safety features are always free. [OnMyLead Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) adds unlimited rides and more.

## I Deleted the Ride I Made This Month. Can I Make Another on Free?

No. A ride counts when it's created, so cancelling or deleting it doesn't give it back, and copying a ride or using **Ride Again** counts as a new ride. Your next free ride opens on the 1st of next month (UTC).

## Will I Be Charged When My Pro Trial Ends?

No. The [Pro Trial](/help/pro-trial) needs no payment and never turns into a paid subscription. Your account moves to Free, and your rides, routes, groups and maps stay.

## My Pro Trial Ended Mid-Month and I Can't Create a Ride. Why?

Rides you created during the trial count toward that month's one free ride.

## Can I Buy Pro or Use a Promo Code on the Website?

No. Subscribing, **Restore Purchases** and promo codes work only in the app on your phone or tablet. Pro bought in the app also works when you sign in on the website.

## Does Deleting My Account Cancel My Pro Subscription?

No. Apple bills Pro, so also cancel it in your Apple subscriptions so you aren't billed again. See [Manage Your Subscription](/help/manage-subscription).

If you bought Pro on Android, Google Play bills it: cancel it in Google Play too.

## Can I Change My Ride's Time or Meeting Point?

Not after it's created. Tap **Copy This Ride** to make a new ride with the same details and route, pick the new day, then cancel the old ride. See [Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride](/help/edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride).

## My Ride Still Says Live. How Do I End It?

Rides don't end on their own. The organizer taps **End Ride for Everyone** on the ride page. Ending a ride stops everyone's location sharing for that ride.

## Why Can't I See the Exact Meeting Spot?

Only riders who have joined see it. Before you join, you see the general area, within about a mile. See [Privacy](/help/privacy).

## Why Isn't My Ride Showing on Find?

Find lists only public rides that are upcoming or live. Private rides never appear there, and rides drop off a few hours after their meeting time. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride).

## Why Do Other Riders See Me as "Rider"?

You haven't picked a ride name yet. Tap **Pick Your Ride Name** on the Rides tab, or your name at the top of **You**. See [Your Ride Name and Profile](/help/ride-name-and-profile).

## Does "Until I Turn It Off" Sharing Ever End?

Yes. Personal shares stop by themselves after 24 hours. A ride share set to **Until I Leave the Ride** ends when the ride ends or you leave it. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).

## Does Live Tracking Work With No Cell Service?

No. Positions only update when a phone has a connection. [Offline maps](/help/offline-maps) keep the map and route on your screen, and riders without service show where they were last seen.

## Can I Use OnMyLead on an iPad or Android Phone?

Yes. OnMyLead is in the App Store for iPhone and iPad, and on Google Play for Android phones and tablets. On a tablet the map fills the screen, see [Use OnMyLead on a Tablet](/help/use-onmylead-on-a-tablet). You can also plan a ride on the website at onmylead.com, see [Create a Ride on the Website](/help/create-a-ride-on-the-website).

 iPhone and Android riders can join the same ride, see each other on the map and chat together.

## How Many Waypoints Can I Add?

Each rider can add up to 100 waypoints to a ride. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

Looking for people to ride with? The **Find** tab shows public rides near you or anywhere in a state. Private rides never show here. You need an invite link or code for those. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).

![Find a Ride, near you or by state](/help/img/find.webp)

## Find Rides Near You

1. Tap the **Find** tab (or **Find a Ride** on the **Rides** tab).
2. Make sure **Near Me** is selected at the top.
3. Allow location if asked. If location is off, tap **Use My Location**, or pick your state instead.
4. Under **How Far Will You Go?**, pick **25 Miles**, **50 Miles**, **100 Miles** or **250 Miles**.

Rides show on the map and in a list under it, nearest first, with how far away each one is.

## Find Rides Near a Place

Planning a trip somewhere else? Search a park, trailhead or town.

1. On the **Find** tab, tap **Search Near a Place**.
2. Type the place and pick it from the results.

The list shows **Rides Near** that place. Tap **Back to Near Me** to go back to rides around you.

## Find Rides in a State

1. On the **Find** tab, tap **By State**.
2. Pick a state.

Rides in that state show soonest first. To switch states, tap the state's name in the corner of the map.

## Use the Map

- Each dot is a ride. Blue dots are upcoming rides. Red, glowing dots are live now.
- Tap a dot to see the ride's name, time and distance, then tap **Open Ride**.
- Move or zoom the map, then tap **Search This Area** to see rides there. To return, tap the button under the map that starts with **Back to**, such as **Back to Rides Near Me**.
- Use the **+** and **-** buttons to zoom, and the location button to recenter the map.
- On a wide screen, such as the website on a computer, the search and the list of rides sit on the left and the map fills the rest of the screen.

:::note
Dots sit on the ride's general meeting area, within about a mile. The exact meeting spot is shown only to riders who join.
:::

## What You'll See

Find shows public rides that are coming up or live right now. Each ride in the list shows its date, time, general area, difficulty, distance and the vehicles welcome. Tap a ride to open its page and join. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).

If there are no rides yet, tap **Create a Public Ride** to start one. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).

:::tip
The **Rides** tab also lists a few upcoming **Public Rides**. Tap **Find Rides on the Map** (or **See All on the Map**, which shows how many there are) to see them all.
:::

OnMyLead is free to download and use. Free accounts can join as many rides as they like, and every safety feature is free on every plan. OnMyLead Pro is for riders who lead a lot of rides and want extras like offline maps and GPX import.

Pro is $4.99 a month or $29.99 a year in the US. Other countries see the price in local currency. Every new account starts with a [free 30-day Pro Trial](/help/pro-trial).

## What's Included

## Always Free

## The Free Monthly Ride

Free accounts create one ride each calendar month.

- The month follows UTC time, so a new month can start a few hours earlier or later than midnight where you live.
- A ride counts when you create it. Deleting or cancelling it doesn't give the ride back.
- Using **Ride Again** to copy a ride counts as creating a ride.
- Rides you create on the website count too.
- Joining other riders' rides is always unlimited.

When you create a ride on a Free account, the Create a Ride screen shows how many you've created this month, like **Rides Created This Month: 0 of 1**. If you've used it, the app tells you the date your next free ride opens, and you can tap **See OnMyLead Pro** or **Not Now**.

## What Each Pro Feature Does

- **Create More Rides:** Pro creates as many rides as you lead.
- **Import GPX Routes:** bring in a track from Gaia, onX or any GPX file. See [Import a GPX Route](/help/import-gpx). Drawing a route on the map stays free, and a route you already imported stays editable.
- **Offline Maps:** download satellite, topo and trail maps so the map keeps working with no signal. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps). Maps already on your phone keep working on Free.
- **Saved Riding Groups:** save your crew, add riders and invite everyone in one tap. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups). Joining a group, its chat and its ride invites stay free.
- **Create Ride Polls:** ask the group a quick question in ride chat. Everyone can still vote on polls for free. See [Ride Polls](/help/ride-polls).
- **Full Ride History:** Free shows your last 5 past rides. Pro shows every ride you've been on. Nothing is ever deleted, so older rides come back if you upgrade.
- **Advanced Trip Planning:** plan several trips at once, start from packing lists, copy trips and link them to rides. One active trip and the fuel check stay free. See [Trip Planner](/help/trip-planner).
- **Advanced Ride Statistics:** moving time, average and top speed, climbing and the group's totals after every ride. Distance and time out stay free.
- **Premium Ride Cards:** share your ride with the Full Stats and Big Number layouts. The standard card stays free.

When you tap something that needs Pro, a short prompt explains it. Tap **See OnMyLead Pro** to see the plans, or **Not Now** to close it.

## See Your Plan

On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**. **Your Plan** shows Free, Pro Trial or Pro. On Free it also shows how many rides you've created this month.

Your plan is saved on your phone, so the app knows it even with no signal.

:::note
Pro is bought in the app on iPhone or iPad through the App Store. Pro you buy there also works when you use OnMyLead on the website.
:::

On Android, Pro is bought through Google Play. Pro belongs to your OnMyLead account, so it works on iPhone, iPad, Android and the website, whichever store you bought it from.

Trail miles burn more fuel than you think. OnMyLead compares a ride's miles with your machine's range from your garage and tells you, in plain words, whether you have enough.

![Fuel range on a machine page](/help/img/vehicle.webp)

## How Range Is Worked Out

Your range is your fuel (tank plus any extra fuel you carry) times your miles per gallon. The check uses the thirds rule: a third out, a third back and a third in reserve.

- **Enough Range**: the ride is within two thirds of your full range, so you keep a reserve.
- **Range Is Tight**: the ride eats into your reserve. Bring extra fuel or plan a fill-up.
- **Not Enough Range**: the ride is longer than your full range. The check says about how many miles short you are.

When you have enough, it also says roughly how much fuel you'll have left at the end.

## Set Up Your Machine

The check needs your machine's tank size and mileage.

1. Open your machine in the Garage and edit it.
2. Under **Fuel and Mileage**, enter **Tank (gal)**.
3. If you carry spare fuel, enter **Extra Fuel (gal)**.
4. Enter **Miles per Gallon**. Use your real-world trail mpg, not the sticker number.
5. Save.

Your machine's page then shows its **Full Range**, **Safe Turnaround** and **Safe Trip** miles. See [Your Garage](/help/garage).

## Where the Ride's Miles Come From

- If the ride has a mapped route, its miles come from the route. See [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).
- If not, the organizer can enter **Route Length (Miles)** when creating the ride, under **Add Route, Difficulty and More**.

A ride with neither has no miles to check against.

## Check Before the Ride

1. Join the ride, open it and tap the **Details** tab.
2. Find the fuel card. Until there's a result, it's called **Your Machine**.
3. Under **Bringing**, pick the machine you're taking, or **None / Riding Along**.
4. Read the result: **Enough Range**, **Range Is Tight** or **Not Enough Range**, with one line of advice.

If you have only one machine with a tank size and mpg, it's checked until you pick one.

You can change your machine while the ride is scheduled or live.

If the card says to add tank size and mpg, tap **Edit Machine**. If your garage is empty, tap **Add Your Machine to the Garage**.

## In Ride Mode

When the ride has a mapped route, Ride Mode shows your range check with the route progress, colored green, yellow or red. It uses the route's length and the machine you picked for the ride. See [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

:::tip
Running low on the trail? Use the **Need Fuel** status button to let the group know. See [Status Buttons](/help/status-buttons).
:::

## Good to Know

- The check is worked out for you from your own garage.
- It's a planning guide, not a gauge. Hills, sand, mud, load and speed all change real fuel use.
- The Trip Planner has a fuel check too. See [Trip Planner](/help/trip-planner).

The Garage keeps your machines in one place: a photo, the details, every part you've added and how far a tank will take you.

![A machine in the Garage with its fuel range and build](/help/img/vehicle.webp)

## Open Your Garage

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Your Gear**, tap **Garage**.

You need to be signed in.

## Add a Machine

1. Tap **Add a Machine**.
2. Under **What Are You Adding?**, pick **Vehicle** or **SXS/UTV**.
3. Tap **Choose Photo** to add a photo from your library (optional).

On Android, the system photo picker opens, and OnMyLead only gets the photo you pick.
4. Fill in a **Nickname**, or the **Year**, **Make** and **Model**. You need a nickname or a make and model. **Trim** is optional.
5. Add the rest if you like: **VIN**, **Purchase Price ($)**, **Engine Hours** and **Odometer (Miles)**.
6. Under **Fuel and Mileage**, enter **Tank (gal)**, any **Extra Fuel (gal)** you carry and **Miles per Gallon**. Use your real-world trail mileage, not the sticker.
7. Tap **Add to Garage**.

## Fill In Details From the VIN

1. Type the 17-character **VIN**.
2. Tap **Fill Year, Make and Model From VIN**.
3. Check the year, make, model and trim it fills in.

If there's no match, enter the details by hand. A VIN is 17 letters and numbers and never uses I, O or Q.

## See Your Fuel Range

Once a machine has a tank size and mpg, its page shows a **Fuel Range** card:

- **Full Range**: how far you can go on your tank plus extra fuel.
- **Safe Turnaround**: a third of your full range. Turn around by this many miles out.
- **Safe Trip**: two thirds of your full range, the longest round trip that still keeps a third in reserve.

It uses the thirds rule: a third out, a third back, a third in reserve. If a machine has no range yet, tap **Add Fuel Range**.

Your Garage also powers the fuel check on a ride. See [Fuel Range](/help/fuel-range).

## Track Your Build

1. Open a machine.
2. Tap **Add a Part or Extra**.
3. Pick the **Area**, like **Wheels & Tires**, **Suspension**, **Lighting** or **Recovery**.
4. Enter the **Item**, and if you like the **Brand**, **Cost ($)**, **Installed** date (like 2026-05-01) and **Notes**.
5. Tap **Add**.

Parts are grouped by area with a subtotal for each. At the bottom you'll see the **Build Total**, and if you entered a purchase price, the **Purchase Price** and **All In** total.

To change or remove a part, tap it, then tap **Save** or **Remove Item**.

## Export Your Build

Under **Export** on a machine's page:

- **Build Sheet** shares your machine and its parts as text, to send in a message or paste anywhere.
- **CSV** saves the build list as a spreadsheet file you can send to Files, email or a spreadsheet app.

## Edit or Delete a Machine

1. Open the machine.
2. Tap **Edit Machine** to change its details or photo, then tap **Save Changes**.
3. Or tap **Delete**, then confirm. The machine and all its build items are removed.

OnMyLead is a group ride app for off-road riders. The leader creates a ride, the crew joins with a code, link or QR code, and on the trail everyone shares one live map, a group chat and quick taps like **Need Fuel** and **Flat Tire** that tell the whole group at once.

## Get the App

OnMyLead runs on iPhone, iPad, Android phones and Android tablets. Download **OnMyLead** free from the App Store on an iPhone or iPad, or from Google Play on an Android phone or tablet, then open it. It's the same account, rides and Pro plan on every device, and iPhone and Android riders ride together on the same map.

## Make Your Account

You can look around without an account, but you need one to create rides, save your Garage and keep riding groups.

1. On the **Rides** tab, tap **Sign In or Create a Free Account**.
2. Tap **Create Account** at the top.
3. Use one of the **Continue with** buttons, or enter **Your Name**, **Email** and a **Password** of at least 8 characters, then tap **Create Account**.
4. If we email you a link, tap it on the same iPhone to confirm your email and finish signing in.

See [Sign In and Create an Account](/help/sign-in) for every way to sign in.

Next, pick your ride name. It's what other riders see on the map, the rider list and in chat. Until you pick one, Home shows **Pick Your Ride Name** and other riders see you as Rider. See [Your Ride Name and Profile](/help/ride-name-and-profile).

New accounts start with a free Pro Trial. See [The Pro Trial](/help/pro-trial).

## Find Your Way Around

Four tabs run along the bottom of the screen.

On a tablet they run down the left edge instead. See [Use OnMyLead on a Tablet](/help/use-onmylead-on-a-tablet).

### Rides

Your home screen.

- **Create a Ride**: start a ride that you lead. Free accounts create one ride a month. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride) and [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
- **Join a Ride**: type an invite code and tap **Open**. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).
- **Find a Ride**: opens the Find tab.
- When one of your rides is live, a card at the top says **Your ride is live. Tap to open Ride Mode**.
- **Ride Invites**, **Your Rides** and **Past Rides** list the rides you're on. Swipe a ride left to delete it (if you organize it) or leave it. The app always asks first.
- **Public Rides** shows a few upcoming public rides near the bottom.

### Find

Public rides on a map. Choose **Near Me** or **By State**, or use **Search Near a Place** to look around a trailhead, park or town. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride).

### Groups

Your riding groups, the groups you're in, and **Leaders You Follow**. Tap **New Group** to save your crew. You need an account for this tab; if you're signed out, it takes you to sign in. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups).

### You

Everything that isn't a ride:

- Your ride name and plan at the top.
- **Your Gear**: [Garage](/help/garage), [Trip Planner](/help/trip-planner) and [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).
- **On the Trail**: **Share My Location** and [Starlink](/help/starlink).
- **Settings**: [Notifications](/help/notification-settings), **Directions** (which maps app **Navigate** opens), **Subscription** and **Blocked Riders**.
- **Account**: the email you sign in with.
- **Help**: **Contact Us** and **Help and Support**.
- **Sign Out** and **Delete Account** at the bottom.

## Permissions the App Asks For

### Notifications

After you sign in, your iPhone asks if OnMyLead can send notifications. Say yes so you hear when someone in your group taps **Need Help** or **EMERGENCY**, even with the phone in your pocket. Tapping a notification opens the ride it is about. You choose everything else in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

### Location

OnMyLead asks for your location when you first use it, for example to find rides near you or when you start sharing on a ride. Your location is shared only with riders you choose, only while you're sharing.

When you share on a ride, your iPhone may also ask to allow location **Always**. Allow it so your group keeps seeing you while your phone is locked on the mount. Sharing always stops when your timer ends or the ride ends. See [Location Sharing](/help/location-sharing).

On Android, allow location **While Using the App**. OnMyLead never asks for **Allow All the Time**: while you share, Android shows a **Sharing Your Location** notification, and that keeps your group updated with the phone locked. On Android 13 and later, allow notifications too, so you can see that notification and hear **Need Help** and **EMERGENCY** alerts.

### Photos

If you add a photo of your machine to your Garage, the app asks to use your photos. Only the photo you pick is uploaded.

## Using the Website

Some things also work at onmylead.com in a web browser:

- Sign in with the same account.
- Create a ride from your computer and draw its route on a big map. See [Create a Ride on the Website](/help/create-a-ride-on-the-website).
- Open a ride with its invite code.
- Send us a message with **Contact Us**.
- On a computer, once you're signed in, **Rides**, **Find**, **Groups** and **You** run down the left side of the page.
- Read these guides: click **Help** at the top of the home page, on a computer or a phone.

Ride Mode and live tracking stay in the app on your phone or tablet.

## Notices From the Team

Sometimes a card at the top of Home shows a message from the OnMyLead team, like **Planned Maintenance** or an announcement. You can close an announcement with its X. A maintenance notice stays until the work is done.

If a screen says something like **Trip Planner Is Off for Now**, that feature is switched off for a while. Everything you saved is kept, and your rides work as usual.

Every riding group has its own chat: a group text for everyone in the group. Use it to plan the next ride or talk about the last one. It's separate from [ride chat](/help/ride-chat), which is for the riders on one ride.

![A riding group chat](/help/img/group-chat.webp)

Group chat is free for everyone in the group. Only the riders in the group can read it or post in it.

## Open the Chat

1. Tap the **Groups** tab.
2. Tap the newest message under a group, or open the group and tap **Group Chat**.

Groups with messages you haven't read show a red count.

## Send a Message

1. Type in the box at the bottom.
2. Tap the send button.

Your message shows **Sending**, then **Sent**. If it can't go through, for example with no signal, it shows **Not Sent**. Tap **Retry** to send it again, or **Remove** to drop it.

Messages can be up to 500 characters. If you send a lot of messages in a row, the app asks you to wait a minute.

## Talk About a Ride

You can tie a message to one of your rides, so everyone knows which ride you mean.

1. Tap **About a Ride** above the message box.
2. Under **Which Ride Is This About?**, pick the ride.
3. Type your message and send it.

The list shows rides you've joined that are happening now, coming up, or ended in the last 30 days. To send without a ride, tap the ride's name above the message box to remove it.

Rides the group has talked about show in a strip at the top of the chat. Tap a ride to see only the talk about it, and tap **Open the Ride** to go to its page. Tap **All Talk** to see every message again.

## Mute a Group

Tap **Mute** at the top of the chat to stop notifications from that group. Tap **Unmute** to turn them back on.

To turn off notifications for all your groups' chats, switch off **Riding Group Chat** in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Clear a Message

- **Your own message:** press and hold it, then confirm **Clear**. It disappears for everyone, and this can't be undone.
- **If you run the group:** press and hold anyone's message and tap **Clear**.

## Report or Block a Rider

Press and hold someone else's message, then tap **Report Rider** or **Block Rider**. Messages from riders you've blocked aren't shown to you. See [Report and Block](/help/report-and-block).

Already have the trail you want to ride as a track in another app? Export it as a GPX file and import it as your ride's route. Riders see it in Ride Mode just like a route drawn in OnMyLead.

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Drawing a route on the map stays free: see [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).

## Import a File

You need to be the ride's organizer or a co-organizer.

1. Open the ride, tap the **Map** tab, and tap **Build the Route** (or **Edit Route**).
2. Tap **Import GPX**.
3. Pick the GPX file. On iPhone it opens your Files, so save the file there first.
4. Check the track on the map. The panel shows its miles and how many track points it has.
5. Tap **Save Route**.

If you're on the Free plan, tapping **Import GPX** shows what Pro includes instead of opening the file picker.

## What Gets Imported

- If the file has a track, the track is used.
- If it has no track, its route is used.
- If it has neither, its waypoints are joined in order.

The track's name from the file is kept with the route. Very long tracks are simplified a little so they load and draw quickly on every rider's phone.

:::note
Waypoints inside a GPX file aren't added as OnMyLead waypoints. To mark camp, fuel or a planned stop, see [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).
:::

## Change an Imported Route

An imported track is shown as it is, so you can't drag or add points to it.

- To use a different file, tap **Clear**, then **Import GPX** again.
- To draw your own instead, tap **Clear** and start tapping the map.

Tapping a line on an imported route's map shows that trail's name and who can ride it. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).

GPX import works with Pro from either store: the App Store on iPhone and iPad, or Google Play on Android.

## If Your Pro Plan Ends

A route you already imported stays on the ride. Importing a new GPX file needs Pro.

## On the Website

**Import GPX** works the same way in the website's route builder. Pick the file from your computer.

## Troubleshooting

- **"That file is not a GPX file."** Go back to the other app, export the track as GPX (not KML or another format) and try again.
- **"That GPX file has no track in it."** The file doesn't have at least two points to draw. Export the track itself, not just a single waypoint.

## Find the Invite Card

Right after you create a ride, its page opens with the invite card at the top. Later, open the ride page and tap **Riders** to find the **Invite Riders** card.

Anyone on a ride can share it, not just the organizer. On a public ride, anyone who can see the ride page can share it. On a private ride, only riders who have joined see the invite card.

## Send the Invite

On the invite card, tap:

- **Share Invite** to send it with any app on your phone
- **Text** to open a new text message
- **Email** to open a new email
- **Copy Link** to copy the ride's link, then paste it anywhere

The message includes the ride name, the link and the invite code. When your friend taps the link, the ride opens in OnMyLead if they have it, or on onmylead.com with a button to get the app.

On Android, ride and riding group links open straight in the OnMyLead app once it's installed.

## Share the Code

The **Invite Code** is shown in big letters on the card. Friends can type it on the **Rides** tab under **Join a Ride**. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).

## Show a QR Code

Tap **Show QR Code** (or the small QR code) to show it full screen, so riders at the trailhead can scan it off your phone. See [QR Codes](/help/qr-codes).

## Invite a Riding Group

Organizers can invite everyone in a riding group at once. Each rider gets a notification and sees the ride on their **Rides** tab, and they join with one tap.

From the ride page:

1. Open the ride page and tap **Riders**.
2. On the invite card, under **Invite a Group**, tap **Invite All** next to the group.

From the group:

1. On the **Groups** tab, open the group.
2. Tap **Invite to a Ride**.
3. Tap the ride. It lists the upcoming rides you organize.

You can also pick groups under **Invite a Group** when you create the ride. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).

:::note
Invited riders skip approval, even on a ride where you approve riders. Saving a riding group is a Pro feature, but inviting a group you're already in to your ride is not. See [Riding Groups](/help/riding-groups) and [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
:::

## Public or Private?

- **Public** rides can also be found by riders near you or in your state on the Find tab.
- **Private** rides are only found by people you send the link, QR code or code to. Anyone holding them can join, so share them only with people you want on the ride.

Joining a ride is free, with no limit on how many rides you join. You need a free OnMyLead account.

## Join With a Link

1. Tap the ride link someone sent you.
2. If you have OnMyLead on your phone or tablet, the ride opens in the app. If not, it opens the ride's page on onmylead.com, with a button to get the app from the App Store or Google Play.
3. Tap **Join Ride**.

If you aren't signed in, the button says **Sign In to Join**. See [Sign In](/help/sign-in).

## Join With a Code

1. On the **Rides** tab, tap **Join a Ride**.
2. Type the invite code, for example 7F3A9C21.
3. Tap **Open**.
4. On the ride page, tap **Join Ride**.

## Join With a QR Code

Point your phone's camera at the ride's QR code and tap the link that appears. See [QR Codes](/help/qr-codes).

## Join From Find

Public rides are listed on the **Find** tab. Open one and tap **Join Ride**. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride).

## Join From a Group Invite

When someone invites your riding group, you get a notification and the ride shows under **Ride Invites** on the **Rides** tab.

1. Tap the ride.
2. In the **You're Invited** card, tap **Join Ride**, or **No Thanks** to turn it down.

You don't wait for approval when you're invited. If you say no thanks, you can still join later with the ride's link or code. On a ride where the organizer approves riders, you then ask to join like anyone else.

## Public and Private Rides

**Public** rides can be found on the Find tab, and anyone can open their page.

**Private** rides (marked **Private, Invite Only**) never show in Find. You need the link, QR code or invite code to see one.

Before you join either kind, the ride page shows the name, time, general area and details. After you join, you also see:

- The exact meeting point, and directions to it
- The organizer's instructions for joined riders
- The route and planned stops
- Who's going
- The ride chat

## After You Join

The ride shows under **Your Rides** on the **Rides** tab. On the ride page you'll find **Details**, **Map**, **Riders** and **Chat** sections. When you get to the meeting spot, tap **I'm Here and Ready** to check in. See [Check In](/help/check-in).

When the organizer starts the ride, tap **Enter Ride Mode**. See [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

If the ride is full, you go on the waitlist. If the organizer approves riders, you wait for them to say yes. See [Approvals and the Waitlist](/help/approvals-and-waitlist).

## Leave a Ride

1. Open the ride page and tap **Riders**.
2. Tap **Leave Ride**.

Or, on the **Rides** tab, swipe left on the ride and tap **Leave**. Your spot opens up for someone else. You can rejoin with the ride's link or code if there's room. If the ride is live, leaving also stops sharing your location with the group.

:::note
You can't join a ride that has ended or been cancelled.
:::

summary: Who rides up front, who rides at the rear, and how to make someone leader, pick a tail gunner or hand off the ride.

---

Every group ride needs someone up front and someone at the back. OnMyLead shows the riding order on the roster: the leader first, the tail gunner last, everyone else in between.

## The Roles

- **Organizer**: the rider who created the ride (or was given it). Runs the ride page, starts and ends Ride Mode, and leads unless someone else is made leader.
- **Leader**: rides up front. Messages sent to the leader in ride chat go to them.
- **Tail Gunner**: rides at the rear so nobody gets left behind. In OnMyLead, the tail gunner is the sweep.
- **Rider**: everyone else.

On the **Riders** section of the ride page, the line at the top of the **Going** list shows who is **Leader** and who is **Tail Gunner** (or "Not picked yet").

## Make Someone Leader

The organizer can put another rider up front while still organizing.

1. On the ride page, tap **Riders**.
2. Tap the rider's name in the **Going** list.
3. Tap **Make Leader**.

To take the lead back, tap their name and tap **Remove as Leader**. You can make more than one rider a leader.

## Pick a Tail Gunner

The organizer or the leader can pick the one rider who rides at the rear.

1. On the ride page, tap **Riders**.
2. Tap the rider's name.
3. Tap **Make Tail Gunner**.

There's only one tail gunner at a time. Picking someone new moves the job to them. To clear it, tap the tail gunner's name and tap **Remove as Tail Gunner**. The leader and organizers ride up front, so they can't also be tail gunner.

## Hand Off the Lead

A rider who was made leader can pass the lead to someone else.

1. On the ride page, tap **Riders**.
2. Tap the rider's name.
3. Tap **Hand Them the Lead**, then **Hand Off**.

They lead from here, messages to the leader go to them, and you stay on the ride as a rider.

## Give Away the Whole Ride

The organizer can hand the entire ride to another rider, for example if you can't make it.

1. On the ride page, tap **Riders**.
2. Tap the rider's name.
3. Tap **Give Them the Ride**, then **Give Ride**.

They become the organizer and the leader. You stay on the ride as a rider and can't undo this yourself.

:::note
Roles can only go to riders who have joined the ride, and they can't change after the ride has ended or been cancelled.
:::

The rider gets a notification when they're made leader, made tail gunner or given the ride.

OnMyLead only shares your location when you turn it on, only with the people you choose, and only for as long as you pick. Every share ends on its own. These rules are enforced by OnMyLead's server, not just the app.

There are two ways to share:

- **With a ride:** everyone on the ride sees you on the Ride Mode map.
- **With chosen people:** riders you pick, a family link, or both, from **Share My Location**.

## Share with Your Ride

When you open Ride Mode on a live ride and aren't sharing yet, the app asks **Share Your Location with This Ride?**

1. Open Ride Mode. See [Use Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).
2. Pick how long to share: **2 Hours**, **4 Hours**, **8 Hours** or **Until I Leave the Ride**.
3. Or type your own length in **Hours** and tap **Share**. The longest you can pick is 24 hours.
4. If your iPhone asks for location access, allow it. Choose **Always** so the group keeps seeing you with the phone locked.

Only riders on this ride see you. Tap **Not Now** to skip. You can start sharing later by tapping the **Off** pill at the top of Ride Mode.

### Check or Stop Ride Sharing

The pill at the top of Ride Mode shows the time left, such as **1h 20m**, or **On** when you picked **Until I Leave the Ride**.

1. Tap the pill. A banner shows **Sharing** and the time left.
2. Tap **Stop** to stop sharing now, or **Hide** to fold the banner back into the pill.

### When Ride Sharing Ends

Sharing with a ride stops on its own at the first of these:

- Your timer runs out.
- The organizer ends or cancels the ride.
- You leave the ride.
- You tap **Stop**.

Closing Ride Mode, or locking your phone, doesn't stop sharing. If the app was closed or your phone restarted, opening Ride Mode picks your share back up.

## Share with Chosen Riders or Family

1. Tap the **You** tab.
2. Under **On the Trail**, tap **Share My Location**.
3. Under **Who Can See You**, tap the riders you want. Only people you've been on a ride with are listed.
4. To share with someone who doesn't have the app, turn on **Family Link**. See [Share a Family Link](/help/family-link).
5. Under **For How Long**, pick **15 Min**, **1 Hour**, **4 Hours**, **8 Hours** or **Until I Turn It Off (Max 24 Hours)**, or type your own length in **Hours** and tap **Share**.

**Until I Turn It Off** still stops by itself after 24 hours, so a forgotten share always ends.

While you share, **Share My Location** shows a card for each share with **Sharing Now** and the time left.

- Tap **Add 1 Hour** to keep going longer. In the last 10 minutes, the button says **Ending Soon · Add 1 Hr**.
- Tap **Stop** to end it now.

## Location in the Background

To keep your group updated while your phone is locked or in your pocket, OnMyLead needs location access set to **Always**. You can change it any time in your iPhone's **Settings > OnMyLead > Location**. While OnMyLead is using your location in the background, iPhone shows its location indicator.

On Android, allow location **While Using the App**. OnMyLead doesn't need **Allow All the Time**. While you share, Android shows a **Sharing Your Location** notification, and that is what keeps your group updated with the phone locked. Tap it to see who can see you or to stop sharing. On Android 13 and later, also allow notifications when asked, or that notification stays hidden.

:::release 1.0.1
If you turn off location for OnMyLead while you're sharing with a ride, Ride Mode shows a **Location Is Off** notice once, because your group can't see you move. Turn location back on for OnMyLead in your phone's **Settings** to keep sharing.
:::

Your phone sends a new position each time you move about 25 meters (80 feet), and at least every 15 seconds while you're stopped, so the group can tell you're still there.

:::release 1.0.1
To make your battery last longer, you can have your phone send less often with [Battery Saver](/help/battery-saver). It starts on **Best Accuracy**, the rate above.
:::

## With No Service

Live tracking needs a connection. When your phone has no service:

- The group sees where you were last seen, with how long ago, never a dot that looks live.
- While you share with a ride, your phone keeps recording your track. When you get service again, your current position goes up, and the points from the dead zone are added to your ride track for your [ride summary](/help/ride-summary-and-ride-again).
- Sharing still ends at its end time, even if your phone can't reach the server.

Offline maps keep the map on your screen without service, but positions only update when phones have a connection. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

## Who Sees What

- **Ride sharing:** riders who have joined that ride.
- **Chosen riders:** only the riders you picked are allowed to see your position.
- **Family link:** anyone who has the link, until the share ends.

Your exact location is never shown publicly. See [Privacy](/help/privacy).

OnMyLead Pro is billed by Apple, so you change or cancel it in your Apple Account settings. The app takes you straight there.

## Cancel or Change Your Plan in the App

1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
2. Tap **Manage Subscription**.
3. Apple's subscription screen opens. Choose a different plan, or cancel your subscription.

If you pay for Pro, the Pro screen also has a **Manage Subscription** button where the plans usually are.

## Cancel or Change It on Android

On Android, Pro is billed by Google Play. **Manage Subscription** opens Google Play's subscription page for OnMyLead, where you can change plans or cancel. You can also do it in the **Play Store** app: tap your profile picture, then **Payments & Subscriptions** > **Subscriptions** > **OnMyLead**.

If you bought Pro on a different kind of device (on an iPhone while you're on Android, or the other way round), **Manage Subscription** tells you which store bills it and opens that store's subscription page. Cancel it there.

## Cancel or Change It in iPhone Settings

1. Open the **Settings** app on your iPhone.
2. Tap your name at the top.
3. Tap **Subscriptions**.
4. Tap **OnMyLead**, then choose a plan or cancel.

:::warning
To avoid being charged for the next period, cancel at least 24 hours before your current period ends. The subscription renews automatically until you turn it off.
:::

## Check When It Renews

On the **Subscription** screen, **Your Plan** shows **Pro** and the date it renews or ends.

## What Happens When Pro Ends

When a subscription you cancelled reaches the end of the period you paid for, your account moves to Free. Nothing is deleted:

- **Rides:** every ride you created stays. Free accounts create one new ride a month.
- **Routes:** routes you already imported from GPX stay and stay editable. Importing a new GPX file needs Pro.
- **Offline maps:** maps already on your phone keep working. Downloading new map areas needs Pro.
- **Riding groups:** your groups stay, with their chats, and you can still invite them to your rides. Creating a group or adding and removing riders needs Pro.
- **Polls:** polls already sent can still be voted on. Creating a new poll needs Pro.
- **Ride history:** Home shows your last 5 past rides. The rest are saved, and show again if you upgrade.
- **Trips:** your trips stay. Free plans one active trip at a time.

See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) for the full comparison.

## Good to Know

- Deleting your OnMyLead account does not cancel the Apple subscription. Cancel it in your Apple subscriptions too, so you aren't billed again. See [Delete Your Account](/help/delete-account).
- If your plan says **Complimentary Pro**, it was given to you by OnMyLead and isn't billed by Apple, so there's nothing to cancel.

- Deleting your OnMyLead account doesn't cancel a Google Play subscription either. Cancel it in Google Play too.
- On Android, **Your Plan** also says which store bills your Pro.
- Subscriptions can only be managed in the app on your phone or tablet. On the website, the Subscription screen says so.

OnMyLead's maps can show public trails and roads over satellite imagery or a topo map. Tap a trail to see its name and which vehicles are allowed on it.

![Trail lines and rider dots on the satellite map](/help/img/map.webp)

## Open the Layers

The layers button is the round button with a stacked layers icon in the top-right corner of the map. You'll find it on:

- Ride Mode's map
- A ride's waypoints map
- The route builder
- The area picker for offline maps

Tap it to open the **Map** panel. Tap it again to close the panel.

Your choices are remembered on your phone and used on every map in the app.

## Satellite or Topo

At the top of the panel, pick:

- **Satellite**: aerial imagery with road and place labels. This is the default.
- **Topo**: the USGS topographic map, with contour lines.

## Public Trails and Roads

Turn **Public Trails and Roads** on to draw trail and road lines on the map. It's on unless you turn it off.

- **Trail**: a dashed sand-colored line.
- **Road**: a solid pale line.

The lines come from:

- **USDA Forest Service**: the Motor Vehicle Use Map roads and trails.
- **Bureau of Land Management**: BLM routes.
- **OpenStreetMap**: tracks mapped by riders, including off-road parks, state land and county roads.

Trail lines show once you zoom in. If you see **Zoom In to See Trails**, zoom in a little. If you see **Zoom In for Park and Local Trails**, the Forest Service and BLM lines are showing, and the OpenStreetMap tracks appear when you zoom in closer.

The map on the **Find a Ride** tab shows trail lines too when you zoom in, following the choice you made here.

## See Who Can Ride a Trail

1. Make sure **Public Trails and Roads** is on and you're zoomed in.
2. Tap a trail or road line. In the route builder, press and hold instead, since a tap adds a route point.
3. A card shows the trail's name, where it is, whether it's a trail, road or track, the segment's miles and surface when known.

Under **Open To**, the card lists the vehicles the agency allows. If access changes by season, it says **Open To, by Season** with the open dates. If the agency data doesn't say, the card tells you.

For an OpenStreetMap track, the card says it was mapped by riders on OpenStreetMap, and that parks and private land need permission or a pass.

:::warning
Map data can be out of date. Always check posted signs and closures before you ride.
:::

## Download a Ride's Map

On a ride with a route, the panel has **Download This Ride's Map**. One tap saves satellite, topo and trails around the route for riding with no signal. This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) and [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

The **Offline Maps** link at the bottom of the panel opens all your downloaded maps.

## With No Signal

When your phone loses signal, a **No Signal** tag with **Downloaded Map** appears under the layers button. The map then shows only what's saved on your phone, and the satellite view switches to downloaded USGS aerial photos. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

## On the Website

The website's maps show satellite imagery only. The layers button, the topo map, the Forest Service and BLM lines and the trail lookup are in the app. When you build a route on the website, OpenStreetMap trail lines appear once you zoom in close.

## Map Data and Credits

- Trails and roads: USDA Forest Service MVUM, Bureau of Land Management, and map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, © OpenMapTiles, served by OpenFreeMap.
- Topo: USGS The National Map.
- Satellite with no signal: USGS The National Map: Orthoimagery.

The credits for what's showing are listed at the bottom of the **Map** panel. Loading map squares only sends the area being looked at, never anything about you.

You decide what OnMyLead tells you about. Every change saves as soon as you make it, and your choices apply on any device you sign in on.

## Open Notification Settings

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Settings**, tap **Notifications**. The line under it sums up your settings, like **Everything on** or **2 turned off**.

## Always On: Help and EMERGENCY

When someone in your group taps **Need Help** or **EMERGENCY**, you're always told, even during quiet hours. This can't be turned off.

## What You Can Turn On or Off

Everything below starts on.

### On the Trail

- **Rider Status**: status buttons and quick replies from Ride Mode, like **On My Way**, **Need Fuel** and **Flat Tire**, and when a rider cancels one.
- **Announcements**: what the organizer tells the whole group.

### Ride Chat

- **Group Chat**: messages and quick replies from your group.
- **Messages to the Leader**: leader-only messages, when you're leading.
- **Show Message Text**: turn this off to keep messages off your lock screen. You'll see who wrote, not what.

### Before the Ride

- **Ride Changes**: a ride starts, is cancelled, or gets a new time or meeting spot, or you get a spot or a role.
- **New Riders**: someone joins or asks to join a ride you organize.
- **Email When a Ride Is Cancelled**: an email as well as the notification if a ride you joined is cancelled or removed.

### Your Riding Groups

- **Ride Invites**: someone invites you, or a group you're in, to a ride.
- **Riding Group Chat**: new messages in your riding groups' chats. To mute just one group, do it from that group's chat. See [Group Chat](/help/group-chat).
- **Leaders You Follow**: a leader you follow posts a new public ride.

### Your Account

- **Pro Trial Reminders**: a week, 3 days and a day before your Pro Trial ends, and when it does.
- **Email Me Too**: the same Pro Trial reminders by email.

## Tapping a Notification

Tapping a notification takes you straight to what it's about, whether OnMyLead was open, in the background or closed:

- A status tap like **Need Help**, a quick reply, or a ride going live opens **Ride Mode** for that ride.
- A ride chat message opens the ride's **Chat**.
- A riding group message opens that group's chat.
- Ride changes, new riders, invites and reminders open the ride.

## Ride Reminder

Get a heads-up before each ride you've joined, with the meeting spot. Under **Ride reminder**, pick **Off**, **30 Min**, **1 Hour**, **2 Hours** or **Day Before**. It starts at **1 Hour**.

## Quiet Hours

1. Under **Quiet hours**, turn on **Silence Overnight**.
2. Use the minus and plus buttons under **From** and **Until** to set the times. Each tap moves the time by half an hour.

During quiet hours everything is held except help alerts. Until you change them, quiet hours run from 10 PM to 6 AM.

## If Notifications Aren't Arriving

- If you see **Notifications Are Off for OnMyLead**, your iPhone is blocking them. Tap **Open iPhone Settings** and turn on **Allow Notifications**.

On Android, the button is **Open Settings**. Android also sorts OnMyLead's notifications into three categories you can tune in **Settings > Apps > OnMyLead > Notifications**: **Rider Alerts** (Need Help, EMERGENCY and other status taps, shown at the highest priority), **Ride Chat** (ride and group chat) and **Ride Updates** (ride changes, new riders, invites, reminders and account notices).
- If you see **Let OnMyLead Send Notifications**, tap **Turn On Notifications** and allow them.
- While OnMyLead is open, new ride chat messages pop up inside the app instead of as a banner.

## On the Website

You can change these settings at onmylead.com too. Notifications themselves come to the app on your phone or tablet.
