---

Out on the trail the signal often drops. Download a map before you leave and the map keeps working with no signal: satellite photos, topo and trail lines for the area you saved.

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Maps already on your phone keep working on the Free plan.

:::warning
Offline maps keep the map, not the tracking. With no signal, your phone can't send or receive positions. Riders show where they were last seen, and positions update again when phones get a connection.
:::

Offline maps are in the app on your phone or tablet only, not on the website.

## Open Offline Maps

- On the **You** tab, tap **Offline Maps**.
- Or, on any map with the layers button, open the layers panel and tap **Offline Maps**.

The screen shows how much space your maps use, how much is free on your phone, your downloads under **On This Phone**, and your upcoming rides under **Your Rides**.

## Download a Ride's Map

The quickest way. It saves satellite, topo and trails around the ride's route.

From Offline Maps:

1. Under **Your Rides**, find the ride. Each one shows about how much space it needs.
2. Tap **Download**.

From the ride's map:

1. Open Ride Mode or the ride's waypoints map.
2. Tap the layers button.
3. Tap **Download This Ride's Map**.

**Your Rides** lists upcoming rides you've joined that have a mapped route. Downloading a ride again replaces its earlier download, which is handy if the route changed.

## Download Any Area

1. On Offline Maps, tap **Download a Map Area**.
2. Move and zoom the map until the frame holds the area you'll ride. The frame's size in miles shows in its corner.
3. Pick the maps to save: **Satellite**, **Topo** and **Trails**. All three are on to start.
4. Check the estimate under the choices.
5. Tap **Download This Area**.

The download is named after the nearest town when your phone can find one.

If you see **Too big for one download. Zoom in a little.**, the area is too large to save with enough detail to ride by. Zoom in, or save it as two downloads.

## Watch and Manage Downloads

Each download on **On This Phone** shows its maps, its size and how it's going.

- **Pause** stops a download for now.
- **Resume** carries on from where it stopped.
- **Finish** appears when some pieces didn't download. The download shows how many are missing; tap **Finish** to try them again.
- **Delete** takes it off your phone. Tap **Delete** again to confirm, or **Keep**.

One download runs at a time. If you close the app during a download, it's paused; open Offline Maps and tap **Resume**.

Deleting a download only removes pieces that no other download also uses, so overlapping maps keep working.

## When the Signal Drops

You don't need to do anything. The app checks for a connection while a map is open. When it can't reach the internet:

- A **No Signal** tag with **Downloaded Map** appears under the layers button.
- The map shows what's saved on your phone. Zoomed in past what you saved, it stretches the closest saved detail.
- The satellite view switches to USGS aerial photos from your download, since the live satellite view can't be saved ahead of time.

The ride's route and waypoints are saved on your phone once you've opened the ride, so they're still on the map too.

:::tip
Download before you leave, while you have good signal. Then open the ride once so its route is on your phone.
:::

## What Gets Saved

- **Satellite**: USGS aerial photos.
- **Topo**: the USGS topo map.
- **Trails**: Forest Service and BLM lines, plus OpenStreetMap tracks (map data © OpenStreetMap contributors).

Trail and topo areas you've already looked at with signal are also kept on your phone for a while, but only a download makes sure the whole area is there.

## If Your Pro Plan Ends

Maps you already downloaded stay on your phone and keep working. Starting a new download needs Pro.

---

When you create a ride, you're its organizer. You're also its leader until you hand that job to someone else. Here's what you can do from your ride page.

## Before the Ride

- **Invite riders.** Share the link, code or QR code, or invite a whole riding group. See [Invite Riders](/help/invite-riders).
- **Approve requests.** If riders asked to join, the **Riders** section shows a red count and a **Waiting for You** list with **Approve** and **Decline**. See [Approvals and the Waitlist](/help/approvals-and-waitlist).
- **Build or edit the route** and add planned stops in the **Map** section. See [Build a Route](/help/route-builder).
- **Pick a leader and a tail gunner** from the roster in **Riders**. See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).
- **Post announcements** in the ride chat. Your latest announcement is pinned near the top of the ride page for everyone on the ride. See [Ride Chat](/help/ride-chat).

You get a notification when someone joins or asks to join a ride you organize. You can turn these off in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Start the Ride

1. Open the ride page.
2. Tap **Start Ride Mode**.

The ride goes live, riders on it get a notification that it started, and Ride Mode opens for you. Everyone else on the ride sees **Enter Ride Mode** on the ride page, and a banner on their **Rides** tab. See [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

## End the Ride

When everyone is off the trail:

1. Open the ride page.
2. In the **You're Organizing** card on **Details**, tap **End Ride for Everyone**.

Ending the ride stops everyone's location sharing for this ride. Riders then see their ride summary on the ride page. See [Ride Summary and Ride Again](/help/ride-summary-and-ride-again).

:::warning
A live ride doesn't end by itself. Remember to tap **End Ride for Everyone** when you're done, so location sharing for the ride stops.
:::

## Hand Off the Whole Ride

If you can't make it, give the ride to another rider who has joined. Open **Riders**, tap their name and tap **Give Them the Ride**. They become the organizer and leader, and you stay on the ride as a rider. You can't undo this yourself. See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).

## Call It Off

Use **Cancel Ride** or **Delete Ride** in the **You're Organizing** card. See [Edit, Cancel or Delete a Ride](/help/edit-cancel-or-delete-a-ride).

## Run It Again

Tap **Copy This Ride** (or **Ride Again** after it ends) to start a new ride with the same details and route. See [Ride Summary and Ride Again](/help/ride-summary-and-ride-again).

:::note
As the organizer you can't leave your own ride. Hand it to another rider first if you need to step away.
:::

---

Wherever OnMyLead asks for a place, you can type its name instead of hunting on a map: a trailhead, an off-road park, a campground, a town or a street address.

## Where You Can Search

- **Creating a ride**: **Search a Place or Address** sets the meeting point, and **Search a Destination** fills in where the ride ends up. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).
- **Find a Ride**: **Search Near a Place** shows rides near the place you pick instead of near you. Tap **Back to Near Me** (or **Clear**) to go back. See [Find a Ride](/help/find-a-ride).
- **Route builder**: **Search** moves the map to a place before you draw. See [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).

## Search

1. Tap the search box and type at least three letters.
2. Results show as you type. Each one says what it is and where, like "Trailhead in Moab, Utah".
3. Tap the one you want.

What happens next depends on where you searched:

- For a meeting point, the coordinates and place name fill in for you. You can still edit the **Place Name**.
- In the route builder, the map moves to the place and marks it. Nothing is added to your route.

If nothing turns up, try the full name, a street address with the town, or a nearby town.

## Search by Coordinates

Type coordinates as latitude and longitude, like `38.5733, -109.5498`, and pick the result. This works for spots that don't have a name.

## Good to Know

- Search covers places in the United States.
- Results near you, or near where the map is looking, come first.
- Search needs a connection. With no signal you'll see **No signal for place search. Try again with service.**
- Only the words you type and a rough area are sent to the search service, never who you are or your exact location.

## On the Website

The same searches work on onmylead.com. When you create a ride on the website, you can also click the map to drop the meeting point and drag the pin to fine-tune it. See [Create a Ride on the Website](/help/create-a-ride-on-the-website).

## Place Data

Places come from OpenStreetMap (map data © OpenStreetMap contributors), searched through Photon, a free service with no account.

---

OnMyLead is built so your location is never public. You choose who sees it and for how long, and sharing always ends. These rules are enforced by OnMyLead's server, not just hidden in the app.

## Before You Join a Ride

Anyone can see a ride's public page: its name, time, description and details such as difficulty and vehicles. What they don't get:

- **The exact meeting point.** Public listings and the ride map show a meeting area rounded to about a mile. The ride page says **Shown after you join**, or **Near** and the area's name.
- **The route, the meeting instructions and the roster.** Only riders who have joined the ride get these.

The exact meeting point and the route are stored separately from the public ride, and the server only hands them to riders on the ride.

## Riders on Your Ride

Once you've joined a ride, the other riders on it can see:

- Your ride name. If you turned on **Show My Google (or Apple or Facebook) Profile**, they also see that account's name and photo. See [Your Ride Name and Profile](/help/ride-name-and-profile).
- That you're on the ride, your role, and whether you've checked in.
- Your messages in the ride chat, except leader-only messages, which only you and the leader can read.
- Your status taps and quick replies from Ride Mode. A status tap carries your phone's location at the moment you tapped it.
- Your live location, but only while you're sharing with the ride.

## Your Live Location

The server only lets someone read your location while all of these are true:

- You have turned sharing on.
- Your share hasn't run out or been stopped.
- They are someone your share covers: a rider on that ride, a rider you picked, or someone with your family link.
- For ride sharing, the ride is still going and you're still on it.

When the ride ends, every ride share on it stops at once. When you leave a ride, your share for it stops. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).

## Your Ride Track

While you share with a ride, your phone keeps a track of where you rode for your ride summary. Only you can see your own track. The group summary shows totals only, never anyone's route.

## Waypoints

Waypoints you drop are only yours, unless you're the ride's leader and choose to share one with the ride. See [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

## Family Links

Anyone with your family link can see your last location until that share ends. See [Share a Family Link](/help/family-link).

## Blocked Riders

When you block a rider, nothing tells them, and they can't see who has blocked them. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

## Your Data

OnMyLead doesn't sell your data or use it for advertising. It shares data only with the services that run the app, such as Apple for notifications and purchases on iPhone. For the full list, read the Privacy Policy at onmylead.com/privacy.

On Android, Google delivers notifications (Firebase Cloud Messaging), handles purchases (Google Play) and draws the map (Google Maps).

You can delete your account and its data at any time. See [Delete Your Account](/help/delete-account).

When you make a new OnMyLead account, you get 30 days of OnMyLead Pro for free. It starts on its own. There's nothing to sign up for and no payment details to enter.

:::tip
You're never charged when the trial ends. It does not turn into a paid subscription. Your account simply moves to Free unless you choose to subscribe.
:::

## See How Many Days Are Left

On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**. **Your Plan** shows **Pro Trial** with the days remaining, the date it ends, and a row of 30 marks that fills in as the days go by.

The trial is the same on Android. It belongs to your account, not your phone, so it shows the same days left on every device you sign in to.

## Trial Reminders

OnMyLead reminds you a week, 3 days and a day before your trial ends, and again when it ends.

- To turn off the notifications, switch off **Pro Trial Reminders** in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).
- The same reminders come by email too. Switch off **Email Me Too** to stop the emails.

## When the Trial Ends

Your account moves to Free. Nothing you made during the trial is deleted:

- Your rides, routes, groups and downloaded maps stay yours.
- New Pro actions, like downloading another map area or importing a GPX file, need Pro again.
- Free accounts create one ride a month. Rides you created earlier in the same month, during the trial, count toward that month.

See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) for exactly what changes.

## Keep Pro After the Trial

1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
2. Tap **Keep Pro After the Trial**.
3. Choose **Annual** or **Monthly**.
4. Tap the **Subscribe for** button under the plans and confirm with Apple.

Apple charges you when you confirm, and your paid subscription starts right away. See [Subscribe to Pro](/help/subscribe-to-pro).

## Good to Know

- Each account gets one trial.
- The trial is part of OnMyLead, not an Apple free trial, so it doesn't show in your Apple subscriptions.

1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
2. Tap **Redeem Promo Code**.
3. Enter your code in Apple's window and follow the steps to confirm.

Apple shows what the code gives you before you confirm. Once Apple accepts the code, OnMyLead checks it and your plan changes to **Pro**. This can take a moment.

That works too. Open OnMyLead afterwards, signed in to your account, with signal. The app picks up the code on its own and turns on Pro.

Every ride has its own QR code. It's the quickest way to get riders on your ride at the trailhead: they point their camera at your screen and they're in.

![A ride QR code with its invite code](/help/img/qr.webp)

## Show Your Ride's QR Code

1. Open the ride page. Right after creating a ride, the invite card is at the top. Later, tap **Riders** to find it.
2. Tap **Show QR Code**, or tap the small QR code on the card.

The QR code opens full screen with the ride name and the invite code under it (**Or Enter Code**), so riders can type the code if their camera won't scan. Tap **Done** to close it.

## Share the QR Code as a Picture

1. Show the QR code full screen.
2. Tap **Share QR Code**.
3. Pick how to send it: text, email or any app.

It sends a picture of the QR code card along with the ride link. You can print it or post it for a club ride.

## Scan a QR Code to Join

1. Open your phone's Camera and point it at the QR code.
2. Tap the link that appears.
3. If you have OnMyLead, you go straight to the ride. If not, the ride's page opens on onmylead.com with a button to get the app.
4. Tap **Join Ride**. See [Join a Ride](/help/join-a-ride).

:::tip
Opened a ride link on your computer? The ride's web page shows its QR code. Scan it with your phone to open the ride there.
:::

:::note
The QR code holds only the ride's link and invite code. It doesn't show the meeting point. On a private ride, anyone who scans it can join, so share it with care.
:::

If a rider or a ride isn't right, report it to the OnMyLead team. If you'd rather not hear from a rider, block them. Neither one tells the other person it was you.

:::warning
If anyone is in danger, call 911 first.
:::

## Report a Rider

1. Open the ride and tap **Riders**.
2. In the **Going** list, tap the rider.
3. Tap **Report Rider**.
4. Under **What's Wrong**, pick **Harassment**, **Unsafe Riding**, **Spam or Scam**, **Fake Account** or **Something Else**.
5. Add details under **Anything Else (Optional)** if you like.
6. Tap **Send Report**.

You can also press and hold one of the rider's messages in ride chat or group chat, then tap **Report Rider**.

## Report a Ride

1. Open the ride's page.
2. Scroll to the bottom and tap **Report Ride**.
3. Under **What's Wrong**, pick **Unsafe Plan**, **Spam or Scam**, **Offensive Content** or **Something Else**.
4. Add details if you like, then tap **Send Report**.

Reports go to the OnMyLead team, not to the rider or the organizer. OnMyLead looks at every report, and the person reported isn't told who sent it.

## Block a Rider

Blocking hides a rider's chat from you.

1. Open the ride and tap **Riders**.
2. In the **Going** list, tap the rider.
3. Tap **Block Rider**.
4. Tap **Block** to confirm.

You can also block from:

- Ride chat or group chat: press and hold their message, then tap **Block Rider**.
- A report: tap **Block This Rider**, or **Also Block This Rider** after you send it.

### What Blocking Does

- You don't see their messages or polls in ride chat or group chat.
- You don't get chat notifications or pop-ups from them.
- They aren't told, and they can't see that you blocked them.

### What Blocking Doesn't Do

- Announcements and Ride Mode quick replies from them still show, because they carry the plan and safety of a ride you're both on.
- Their Need Help and EMERGENCY alerts always come through.
- It doesn't remove them from a ride or stop them seeing you on a ride you're both on. If you're worried about your safety on a ride, leave the ride or stop sharing your location. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).

## Unblock a Rider

1. Tap the **You** tab.
2. Under **Settings**, tap **Blocked Riders**.
3. Tap **Unblock** next to the rider.

You can also tap the rider in a ride's **Going** list and tap **Unblock Rider**.

If you pay for OnMyLead Pro but your plan shows Free, for example on a new iPhone or after reinstalling the app, use **Restore Purchases**. It finds your Pro subscription with Apple and turns Pro back on.

## Restore Your Subscription

1. Sign in to your OnMyLead account.
2. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
3. Tap **Restore Purchases**.
4. If Apple asks, sign in with the Apple Account you used to buy Pro.

When it works, the app says **Your Pro subscription is restored.** and your plan shows **Pro**.

You can also tap **Restore Purchases** at the bottom of the Pro screen.

## If It Says No Purchase Was Found

The app says **No OnMyLead Pro purchase found for this Apple ID.** when the Apple Account on this iPhone has no active OnMyLead Pro subscription. Check that:

- You're signed in to the same Apple Account you used to subscribe.
- The subscription is still active. Look in iPhone **Settings** > your name > **Subscriptions**.
- You have signal.

## Restore on Android

On Android, **Restore Purchases** looks for OnMyLead Pro on the Google account signed in to the Play Store. If it finds none, the app says **No OnMyLead Pro purchase found for this Google account.** Check that the Play Store is signed in to the Google account you used to subscribe, and that the subscription is still active in the **Play Store** app under **Payments & Subscriptions** > **Subscriptions**.

You don't need to restore on a different kind of device. Pro bought on an iPhone shows on your Android phone or tablet as soon as you sign in to the same OnMyLead account, and the other way round.

## One Subscription, One Account

An Apple subscription gives Pro to one OnMyLead account at a time. If you restore it while signed in to a different OnMyLead account, Pro moves to that account. Make sure you're signed in to the account you want Pro on before you tap **Restore Purchases**.

:::note
Restore Purchases works in the app only, on iPhone, iPad or Android. Once Pro is on your account, it also works when you use OnMyLead on the website.
:::

articles.title: Keep the Group Together with Ride Bubble
articles.summary: Ride Bubble watches for riders who drop back, run ahead or stop moving, and warns the leader and tail gunner before anyone gets lost.
articles.text:
---
title: Keep the Group Together with Ride Bubble
summary: Ride Bubble watches for riders who drop back, run ahead or stop moving, and warns the leader and tail gunner before anyone gets lost.
category: ride-mode
order: 30
release: "1.0"
updated: 2026-10-15
sources:
  - app/src/core/bubble.ts
  - app/src/app/ride/[id]/live.tsx
  - app/src/app/ride/new.tsx
  - app/src/components/rider-pin.tsx
  - app/src/components/group-map.tsx
related: [ride-mode, leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner, status-buttons, create-a-ride, location-sharing]
keywords: [bubble, separated, together, left behind, gap, distance alert, stopped rider, tight trail, desert, highway, tablet]
---

Ride Bubble keeps an eye on the gaps in the group while Ride Mode is open. When a rider gets too far from everyone else, stops while the group keeps moving, or goes quiet, Ride Bubble flags them. It's free on every plan.

## How It Decides

Each rider is measured against the nearest other rider, not just the leader. That way a rider who has run far ahead counts too, and the tail gunner at the back is measured against the last rider rather than the whole pack.

A rider turns yellow or red when:

- **They're too far from the nearest rider.** The distances depend on the ride's Ride Bubble setting (below).
- **They've stopped while at least half the group is moving.** Yellow after 2 minutes stopped, red after 5 minutes.
- **Their phone has gone quiet.** No update for 5 minutes turns a rider red, with a message like "No update from Sam for 6 minutes. Showing last known location."

Only riders who are sharing their location are part of Ride Bubble. A rider who isn't sharing can't be measured.

## Ride Bubble Settings

The organizer picks the setting when creating the ride, under **Add Route, Difficulty and More**, in **Ride Bubble**.

| Setting | Yellow when the nearest rider is more than | Red when the nearest rider is more than |
|---|---|---|
| **Standard** | 0.5 miles | 1.5 miles |
| **Tight Trail** | 0.1 miles | 0.25 miles |
| **Desert** | 0.75 miles | 2 miles |
| **Highway** | 1 mile | 3 miles |

The stopped and no-update times are the same for every setting.

## What Everyone Sees

- A yellow or red ring around a rider's dot on the map.
- At the top of Ride Mode, **Together** in green, or the number of red riders, such as **2 Separated**, in red. Tap it to see every rider and when they last updated.

## What the Leader and Tail Gunner See

The ride's leader, tail gunner, organizer and co-organizers also get:

- **An alert card** for each yellow or red rider, such as "Mike is 1.7 miles behind the group. Last moving 4 minutes ago." Tap **Navigate** for directions to them. Leaders and organizers can also tap **Regroup** to set a regroup point at their location.
- **A spoken alert and a buzz** the moment a rider turns red, so you don't have to look down.

The alert cards hide when the bottom panel is folded. Tap **Buttons ▲** to open the panel and see them.

:::note
Spoken alerts pause while your own phone has no service. When you lose signal everyone looks quiet, and that's your signal dropping, not theirs.
:::

## Tips

- Ask everyone to share their location for the whole ride so Ride Bubble can see them. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).
- Give someone the tail gunner role so the back of the group is covered. See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).

Every ride has its own chat for the riders on it. Use it to plan before the ride and check in after. Only riders who have joined the ride can read or post in it.

![Ride chat with polls](/help/img/chat.webp)

:::warning
Don't type while driving or riding. In Ride Mode, use the one-tap quick replies instead. See [Send a Status or Quick Reply](/help/status-buttons).
:::

## Open Ride Chat

1. Open the ride from the **Rides** tab.
2. Tap **Chat** in the row of sections under the ride's name.

Tap **Ride Chat** at the top of the card to hide or show the messages. Hidden, it shows the message count and the latest message. The chat shows the newest 30 messages. To see older ones, tap the button above them, such as **Show 12 Earlier**.

## Send a Message

1. Under **Send To**, pick who it's for:
   - **Everyone:** every rider on the ride.
   - **Leader Only:** only you and the ride's leader see it. The leader's name is shown on the option.
2. Type in the **Message** box.
3. Tap **Send to Everyone** or **Send to Leader**.

Your message shows in the chat straight away as **Sending…**, then **Sent**. If it doesn't go through, it stays as **Not Sent** with **Retry** and **Remove**.

Messages can be up to 500 characters. If you send more than 10 messages in a minute, you're asked to wait a minute.

:::note
The ride's leader is every rider with the Leader role. If nobody has been given that role, the organizer leads. Leader-only messages are kept private by the server, not just hidden in the app. If you're the leader, you won't see the **Leader Only** option.
:::

## Post an Announcement

Organizers and co-organizers can post an announcement for the whole group.

1. Under **Send To**, pick **Announcement (Pinned, Read Aloud)**.
2. Type in the **Announcement** box.
3. Tap **Post Announcement**.

The newest announcement is pinned near the top of the ride page. In Ride Mode it shows as a yellow banner and is read aloud, so riders don't have to look at their phones. Tap the banner to hear it again.

## Clear or Resolve Your Own Message

1. Tap **•••** next to a message you sent.
2. Choose one:
   - **Mark Resolved:** the message gets a green **Resolved** tag for everyone. Tap **Reopen** to undo it. Marking your latest announcement resolved takes it off the pinned spot.
   - **Clear:** removes the message from the ride chat for everyone. Tap **Clear** again to confirm. This can't be undone.

Only the person who sent a message can clear it or mark it resolved.

## Quick Replies in Chat

Quick replies sent from Ride Mode, like **On My Way**, also show in the ride chat in italics.

## Message Pop-Ups

When a new message arrives on a ride you're on, a pop-up slides in at the top of the screen, whatever screen you're on.

- Tap the pop-up to open the ride.
- Tap **Dismiss** to close it. When several are waiting, it shows **+2 More** and **Dismiss All**.
- Pop-ups close on their own after a few seconds, and announcements stay up a little longer.
- If the sender clears a message or marks it resolved before you see it, its pop-up goes away.

Pop-ups and notifications follow your choices in **Notifications**. See [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Report or Block Someone in Chat

Press and hold someone else's message, then tap **Report Rider** or **Block Rider**. See [Report or Block a Rider](/help/report-and-block).

title: Ride Day and Weather
summary: See the forecast for the meeting area and check whether your ride gets back before sunset, right on the ride page.
category: rides
order: 60

related: [create-a-ride, directions, fuel-range, emergency-and-safety]
keywords: [weather, forecast, rain, wind, temperature, sunset, sunrise, daylight, dark, countdown, storm, tablet]
---

The **Ride Day** card on the ride page shows the weather for the meeting area and how your ride lines up with daylight, so nobody gets surprised by a storm or the last miles in the dark.

## Where to Find It

Open the ride page. **Ride Day** is in the **Details** section. It shows on upcoming and live rides.

## The Forecast

Ride Day shows the meet day's forecast:

- The conditions, such as Clear, Partly Cloudy, Rain or Thunderstorms
- The high and low temperature
- The chance of rain
- The wind speed, and gusts when they're much stronger than the wind

The forecast shows up about two weeks before the ride. Until then the card says when it will appear. The forecast is for the ride's general meeting area, not the exact spot.

:::tip
The last forecast your phone loaded is saved, so it still shows at a trailhead with no signal. It only updates when you have a connection.
:::

### Weather Warnings

Ride Day adds a heads-up when the forecast calls for:

- Thunderstorms (watch for lightning and flash floods in washes)
- A 60% or higher chance of rain
- Gusts of 35 mph or more
- A high of 100°F or more
- A low of 32°F or below

## Daylight Check

Ride Day shows sunrise and sunset at the meeting area, with a bar that shows when the ride runs against the daylight.

If the ride has a **Back By** time (the **Expected Finish** you set when creating the ride), Ride Day tells you:

- How long before sunset the group is back
- When it's cutting it close: back less than 45 minutes before sunset
- When the group will be back after dark, with a reminder to bring lights

If there's no finish time, the card says to add a Back By time so it can check it against sunset.

## Countdown

At the top of an upcoming ride's page, a tag counts down to the meeting time, such as "Tomorrow", "In 4 Days" or "Starts in 25 min".

summary: The live group map for ride day. See every rider, who is live and who was last seen, where you are on the route, and the one-tap buttons.

---

Ride Mode is the screen you use on the trail. It puts the whole group on one map, shows how fresh each rider's position is, places everyone along the route, and gives you big one-tap buttons for telling the group what's going on. Ride Mode is free on every plan.

![Ride Mode with the route strip and status buttons](/help/img/live.webp)

## Open Ride Mode

Ride Mode opens once the organizer starts the ride.

- **Organizers:** on the ride page, tap **Start Ride Mode**. The ride goes live for everyone and Ride Mode opens.
- **Riders:** once the ride is live, open the ride page and tap **Enter Ride Mode**. Riders on the ride also get a notification when the ride starts.

The first time you open Ride Mode on a ride, it asks **Share Your Location with This Ride?** Pick how long to share, or tap **Not Now**. You can see the group without sharing, but the group can't see you. See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).

:::tip
Your screen stays on while Ride Mode is open, so the map is ready when you glance at it. Keep a charger handy on long rides.
:::

## What's on the Screen

### The Top Bar

- **‹ Ride name:** tap it to go back to the ride page.
- **The sharing pill:** shows how long you have left sharing, such as **1h 20m**, or **On** when there's no timer. It says **Off** when you aren't sharing; tap it to start. While you share, tap it to show **Sharing, 1 hr 20 min left** with **Stop** and **Hide**.

:::release 1.0.1
If you've turned on [Battery Saver](/help/battery-saver), that banner also names the setting, such as **Sharing, 1 hr 20 min left · Balanced**.
:::

- **Together** or **2 Separated:** green when the group is together, red with a count when [Ride Bubble](/help/ride-bubble) sees riders who have dropped away. Tap it to open the **Riders** list.

### The Map

The map shows the ride's route, waypoints, planned stops and any regroup point. Every rider who is sharing shows as a dot with their ride name beside it. The leader is the one bigger blue dot, so you can find them at a glance. Tap a rider's dot to see their name, whether they're live, and their latest status.

You don't need to leave Ride Mode to see new riders. Someone who joins the ride while you're on the map appears within a few seconds of starting to share, and a rider whose share ends or who leaves the ride drops off the map within about 15 seconds.

To switch map layers or download the ride's map for riding with no signal, use the layers button on the map. See [Map Layers](/help/map-layers) and [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

### The Bottom Panel

The panel at the bottom holds the route strip, alert cards, the quick replies and the status buttons. See [Status Buttons and Quick Replies](/help/status-buttons).

Above the panel are two buttons: **Directions** (on the left) for Apple Maps or Google Maps, and **Add Waypoint** (on the right) to mark your spot. You can also press and hold anywhere on the map to drop a waypoint there. See [Get Directions](/help/directions) and [Waypoints and Planned Stops](/help/waypoints-and-planned-stops).

On Android, **Directions** opens Google Maps, and while you share, a **Sharing Your Location** notification stays in the notification shade. Tap it to come back to OnMyLead. If your phone restarted or the app was updated while you were sharing, opening Ride Mode starts that notification and your sharing again.

## Read the Rider Dots

A dot only looks live when the phone behind it is actually checking in. A sharing phone sends its position at least every 15 seconds while it has service, even when it's parked.

| What you see | What it means |
|---|---|
| Solid dot | Live. The position is less than a minute old. |
| Hollow dot with **Last Seen 2 Min Ago** | Where the rider was last seen, a minute or more ago. |
| Dashed grey ring with **No Signal, 8 Min Ago** | Nothing for three minutes or more. Their phone has likely lost service or stopped sending. |
| Faint ring, **Not Sharing** | The rider is on the ride but isn't sharing their location. |
| Yellow or red ring around a dot | Ride Bubble thinks the rider is separating from the group. |
| Amber wrench on a dot | The rider tapped **Mechanical Issue**. |

## See Every Rider

Tap **Together** (or **Separated**) at the top to open the **Riders** list. It shows everyone on the ride, the leader first, with **Live**, **Last Seen** and an age, **No Signal**, or **Not Sharing**. The leader and tail gunner are labeled.

Tap **Navigate** next to a live rider, or **Go to Last Seen** for a rider whose spot is old, to get directions to them in your maps app.

## See Where You Are on the Route

When the ride has a route, the route strip at the bottom shows the whole route as one straight line from start to finish, with each rider placed by how far along they are. It shows your miles so far, such as **12.3 of 40.1 mi**, and how far you have to go. Below the line it tells you where you stand, for example "The leader is 0.4 miles ahead" or "2 riders ahead of you, 1 behind", and warns you if you're off the route.

If you've added your machine in the [Garage](/help/garage) with its fuel details, the strip also says whether your range covers the route. See [Fuel Range](/help/fuel-range).

## Fold the Panel to See More Map

Swipe the bottom panel down, or tap **Hide ▼** on its handle, to fold it away. Swipe up or tap **Buttons ▲** to bring it back. The app remembers your choice.

While the panel is folded:

- **Mechanical Issue** and **EMERGENCY** stay on screen.
- Need Help and EMERGENCY calls from other riders stay on screen. The leader, tail gunner and organizers also keep Mechanical Issue calls.
- Other alerts are counted in a badge on **Buttons ▲**.

On a tablet the map fills the screen. The **Riders** list sits on the left (tap **Hide** or swipe it left to fold it, **Show Riders** to bring it back) and the buttons panel on the right. See [Use OnMyLead on a Tablet](/help/use-onmylead-on-a-tablet).

## When You Lose Service

If your phone can't reach the server for a short while, a banner says **No Service. Riders Show Where They Were Last Seen**. Everyone else's dots switch to last seen with their ages, because your phone can't hear new positions. If you're sharing, the banner adds that yours sends when service returns.

:::warning
Live positions only update when a phone has a connection. With an offline map downloaded, you keep the map and the route on screen with no signal, but other riders' dots don't move until your phone, and theirs, get service again.
:::

Status taps and quick replies you make with no service wait on your phone and send on their own when you get signal.

## Leave Ride Mode

Tap **‹ Ride name** at the top to go back to the ride page. Leaving the screen doesn't stop sharing: your location keeps going to the group until your timer runs out, the ride ends, you leave the ride, or you tap **Stop**.

Opened Ride Mode by tapping a notification? Tap **‹ Ride name** (or Android's Back) to go to **Home**.

Your ride name is how the group knows you. It shows on the group map, the rider list and in ride chat. A nickname works fine.

## Pick or Change Your Ride Name

1. Go to the **You** tab and tap your name at the top. If you haven't picked one yet, it says **Pick Your Ride Name**. You can also tap **Pick Your Ride Name** on the **Rides** tab.
2. Type your name in **Ride Name**.
3. Check the preview at the top. It shows your pin on the map and a chat line, the way the group sees you.
4. Tap **Save Name**. The button changes to **Name Saved**.

Until you pick a name, other riders see you as Rider.

:::tip
Keep it to 24 characters or fewer so it fits on the map. Extra spaces are tidied up when you save.
:::

## Where Your Name Comes From at First

If you created your account with your name, or signed in with Apple, Google or Facebook, your ride name may already be filled in from that. You can change it any time.

## Show Your Apple, Google or Facebook Profile

If you signed in with Apple, Google or Facebook, you can let the riders you ride with see that account's name and photo. It helps people recognize who joined.

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Account**, find **Show My Google Profile** (or **Show My Apple Profile** or **Show My Facebook Profile**, depending on how you signed in).
3. Turn the switch on.

When it's on, your photo replaces your initial, and a line like "Your Name on Google" shows under your ride name in a ride's rider list and in your riding groups.

When it's off, nobody else sees it. It's off until you turn it on.

### Who Can See It

- Only riders who have been on a ride with you or share a riding group with you.
- Never strangers browsing public rides.
- Never someone you've blocked, or who has blocked you.

The name and photo come from the account you signed in with, and the app keeps them up to date each time you open the **You** tab. You can only turn the setting on or off.

If you signed in with email only, this setting doesn't appear.

## Your Email

Under **Account** on the **You** tab, **Email** shows the email on your account. Only you see it.

A ride poll is a quick question in the ride chat with a few choices. Every rider on the ride gets one vote, can change it, and sees the live counts.

![Polls in ride chat](/help/img/chat.webp)

## Who Can Post a Poll

The ride's leader, the organizer and co-organizers can post polls. Every rider on the ride can vote.

Creating a poll: This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). On a Free plan, picking **Quick Poll** shows **Create Ride Polls**, marked Pro, instead of the poll form. Voting stays free for everyone.

## Post a Poll

1. Open the ride and tap **Chat**.
2. Under **Send To**, pick **Quick Poll**.
3. Tap a starter to fill it in, or type your own:
   - **Lunch Stop?** (Yes, No)
   - **How's the Pace?** (Too Slow, Just Right, Too Fast)
   - **Saturday or Sunday?**
   - **Morning or Afternoon?**
4. Type or edit the **Question**.
5. Fill in **Choice 1** and **Choice 2**. Tap **Add Choice** for more, or **Remove** to drop one.
6. Tap **Post Poll**.

The poll shows in the chat for everyone, and riders get a pop-up saying "Poll from" your name.

### Poll Limits

- 2 to 5 choices, each different.
- The question can be up to 200 characters.
- Each choice can be up to 60 characters.

## Vote

1. Open the ride and tap **Chat**.
2. Tap a choice. It's marked **Your Vote**.

To change your vote, tap another choice. Each choice shows its count and a bar for its share of the votes, and the leading choice is shaded darker. Under the choices you'll see the total, such as **3 Votes**, or **No Votes Yet**.

## Remove a Poll

The person who posted the poll can tap **•••** next to it and tap **Clear**. The poll and its votes are removed for everyone.

When the organizer ends a ride, everyone who was on it gets a summary on the ride page. Organizers can also start the same ride again with one tap.

## See Your Ride Summary

1. On the **Rides** tab, find the ride under **Past Rides**.
2. Tap it. The summary is at the top of the ride page.

The summary has three parts.

### Your Ride

Your **Distance** and how long you were **Out For**, plus a map of your route. Only you can see your route.

Your stats come from sharing your location in Ride Mode. If you didn't share, there's no track for you on that ride. See [Location Sharing](/help/location-sharing).

**Moving Time**, **Average Speed**, **Top Speed** and **Climbing** are part of Advanced Ride Statistics. This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Your full stats are saved either way.

### The Group

Who finished the ride: the riders still on it when it ended. With Pro, you also see the group's totals: the **Longest** and **Average** distance and the **Group Top Speed**. These are totals only, and nobody's route is shown.

### Ride Card

A picture of the ride to share with friends or on social media.

1. Pick a layout: **Standard**, **Full Stats** or **Big Number**.
2. Tap **Share Ride Card**.

**Standard** is free. **Full Stats** and **Big Number** are Premium Ride Cards. This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). The card never shows the meeting point or anyone's route.

## Ride Again

Organizers can set up the same ride again without filling everything in.

1. Open the ended ride's page.
2. In the **You're Organizing** card, tap **Ride Again**.
3. The Create a Ride form opens with the name, details, meeting point and route already filled in. The day is set to the next one on the same weekday.
4. Check the day and times.
5. Tap **Create Public Ride** or **Create Private Ride**.

On a ride that hasn't ended yet, the same button is called **Copy This Ride**.

:::note
Ride Again creates a new ride, so it counts toward your monthly rides on Free. See [Create a Ride](/help/create-a-ride).
:::

Advanced Ride Statistics, Premium Ride Cards and full ride history work with Pro from either store: the App Store on iPhone and iPad, or Google Play on Android.

## Past Rides

Ended and cancelled rides move to **Past Rides** on the **Rides** tab. Free shows your last 5. Full ride history is a Pro feature. Nothing is deleted, so older rides show again with Pro. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

To remove a ride from your Past Rides, swipe left on it and tap **Leave** (or **Delete** if you organized it).

A riding group is your regular crew, saved once. When you create a ride, you can invite everyone in the group in one tap instead of sending the invite to each rider. Each group also has its own [Group Chat](/help/group-chat).

Your groups live on the **Groups** tab, on the **Riding Groups** screen. It shows **Your Groups** (the ones you run) and **Groups You’re In** (the ones someone else runs).

:::note
This is a Pro feature. You need Pro to create a group and to add or remove riders. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro). Joining a group with its link, the group chat, inviting a group to your rides and getting the group's ride invites are free for everyone.
:::

## Create a Group

1. Tap the **Groups** tab.
2. Tap **New Group**.
3. Type a **Group Name**, like Saturday Crew. Names can be up to 60 characters.
4. Under **Add Riders You’ve Ridden With**, tick the riders you want in the group.
5. Tap **Save Group**.

The list only shows people you have been on a ride with, the ones you ride with most at the top. If nobody shows up yet, save the group anyway and send friends the group link (see below).

A group holds up to 100 riders.

## Invite Friends With the Group Link

The group link is for friends who aren't on OnMyLead yet, or anyone you haven't ridden with. Anyone in the group can share it.

1. On the **Groups** tab, tap the group.
2. Scroll to **Invite by Link**.
3. Tap **Share Group Link**, or tap **Text**, **Email** or **Copy**.

When your friend opens the link, they see the group's name, who runs it and how many riders are in it. They don't see who the riders are until they join. They tap **Join Group**, or **Create a Free Account to Join** if they don't have an account yet.

:::tip
If a link got shared somewhere it shouldn't, the rider who runs the group can tap **Make a New Link**. The old link stops working, and everyone already in the group stays in.
:::

## Add More Riders

If you run the group:

1. Open the group.
2. Tap **Add Riders You’ve Ridden With**.
3. Tick the riders and tap **Add Riders**.

## Invite Your Group to a Ride

You can invite a group you're in to any upcoming ride you organize or co-organize. There are two ways.

From the group:

1. Open the group.
2. Tap **Invite to a Ride**.
3. Tap **Invite** next to the ride.

From the ride:

1. Open the ride and go to **Riders**.
2. Under **Invite a Group**, tap **Invite All** next to the group.

Everyone in the group gets a notification and sees the ride under **Ride Invites** on their home screen. They can tap **Join Ride**, with no waiting for approval, or **No Thanks**. Riders who are already on the ride, waiting, or who said no thanks are left alone.

To get these invites, keep **Ride Invites** on in [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Rename a Group

If you run the group, open it, tap the group's name, type the new name and tap **Save Name**.

## Remove a Rider, Leave or Delete a Group

- **Remove a rider:** if you run the group, tap **Remove** next to the rider. They stop getting the group's ride invites. You can add them back later.
- **Leave a group:** open the group and tap **Leave Group**. The group link brings you back if you change your mind.
- **Delete a group:** if you run the group, tap **Delete Group**. The group goes away for everyone in it. Rides you already invited it to stay as they are.

## Who Can See a Group

A group's name and who is in it are only visible to the rider who runs it and the riders in it. The group link only shows the name, who runs it and how many riders are in it.

If your Pro ends, your groups stay. Everyone in them can still chat, and you can still invite the group to your rides. Creating new groups and adding or removing riders needs Pro again.

A route is the line your group will follow. Once it's saved, every rider on the ride sees it on the ride page and in Ride Mode, with everyone placed along it. You draw it by tapping points on a satellite map, and OnMyLead follows the trails between your taps for you.

Drawing a route is free. Bringing one in from a GPX file is covered in [Import a GPX Route](/help/import-gpx).

## Who Can Draw the Route

The ride's organizer and any co-organizers can build or change the route, until the ride has ended or been cancelled. Everyone else on the ride sees the finished route but can't change it. See [Organizer Controls](/help/organizer-controls).

## Open the Route Builder

When you create a ride and pick **Mapped** under **The Route**, the route builder opens as soon as the ride is created.

To open it later:

1. Open the ride and tap the **Map** tab.
2. Tap **Build the Route**. If the ride already has a route, tap **Edit Route**. For a Freeride, tap **Map a Route Anyway**.

:::note
A Freeride that gets a saved route becomes a mapped ride.
:::

## Draw Your Route

The map opens at the ride's meeting point.

1. Tap the map where the ride starts. That's point 1, shown in green.
2. Tap further along the trail. The route follows the trail between your two taps.
3. Keep tapping along the way. Each new point is numbered, and the last one is shown in white.
4. Watch the miles add up at the top of the panel at the bottom of the screen.
5. Tap **Save Route** when you're done.

After you save, you're taken back to the ride. Only riders on this ride can see the route.

### Follow Trails or Straight Line

Two choices in the panel decide how the next points are joined:

- **Follow Trails**: each tap lands on the nearest trail or road, and the line between taps runs along it. While it works this out you'll see a dashed straight line and **Finding the trail…**.
- **Straight Line**: draws straight from point to point. Use it for open ground, a wash or a park nobody has mapped.

You can switch between them as you go. Points you already placed keep the way they were drawn. The app remembers your choice for next time.

If no mapped trail joins two points, that part is drawn as a straight line and the app tells you so. Add a point on the trail, or zoom in and try again. Points very far apart are also joined with a straight line, so tap more often on long stretches.

:::tip
Trails come from OpenStreetMap, so snapping works best where riders have mapped the trails. Zooming in before you tap helps each point land on the trail you meant.
:::

### Fix Mistakes

- **Undo** takes back the last point.
- Drag any numbered point to move it. If the line next to it was following a trail, it snaps again.
- **Clear** removes every point. Nothing is saved until you tap **Save Route**.

To see more of the map, swipe the panel down or tap its handle. It folds down to the miles and an **Undo** button.

## Search for a Place

To jump the map to a trailhead, park, forest or town before you draw:

1. Tap **Search** at the top of the screen.
2. Type a name, an address or coordinates.
3. Tap a result. The map moves there and marks it.

Searching only moves the map. Nothing is added to your route. See [Search for a Place](/help/place-search).

## Check Who Can Ride a Trail

While drawing, a tap adds a point, so press and hold a trail line instead to see its name and which vehicles it's open to. You can also turn trail lines on or off and switch to a topo map with the layers button. See [Map Layers and Trails](/help/map-layers).

## Change or Remove a Route

1. Open the ride, tap the **Map** tab, and tap **Edit Route**.
2. Move, add or undo points, then tap **Save Route**.

To take the route off the ride, tap **Clear**, confirm, then tap **Remove Route**.

When you save a route, the ride's listed miles update to match it.

## On the Website

You can build the route at onmylead.com too, using the same steps:

- Click the map instead of tapping, and drag a point to move it.
- Press Ctrl+Z (Cmd+Z on a Mac) to undo the last point.
- Trail lines appear once you zoom in close, and **Follow Trails** snaps to them the same way.
- On a wide screen, the tools panel sits beside the map.

On a tablet held sideways, the tools panel sits beside the map; swipe it up or tap **Hide** to fold it. Held upright, it floats in the bottom corner of the map.

The website's map doesn't have the layers button, the topo map or the trail lookup. Those are in the app. A route you save on the website is in the app as soon as you save it.

## No Signal

Once you've opened a ride with a route, the route is saved on your phone, so it's still there without signal. With no signal, **Follow Trails** can only use trail data already saved on your phone, so in other places it draws straight lines. Saving a route needs a connection.

## Map Data

Trail lines and snapping use map data © OpenStreetMap contributors, © OpenMapTiles, served by OpenFreeMap. Snapping is worked out on your phone or in your browser. Your taps aren't sent to a routing service.

---

You need an account to create rides, keep a Garage and save riding groups. You can sign in with a social account, with your email and a password, or with a link we email you.

## Open the Sign-In Screen

1. On the **Rides** tab or the **You** tab, tap **Sign In or Create a Free Account**.
2. At the top, choose **Sign In** if you already have an account, or **Create Account** if you're new.

Tapping something that needs an account, like the **Groups** tab, also opens this screen.

## Sign In With Apple, Google or Facebook

Depending on what's turned on, you'll see **Continue with Apple**, **Continue with Google** and **Continue with Facebook** at the top of the screen.

1. Tap the button for the account you want to use.
2. Follow the steps on the Apple, Google or Facebook screen.
3. You're signed in and taken back to OnMyLead. If you were new, your account is created.

With Apple, the name on your Apple Account is used as your ride name the first time you sign in, if Apple shares it. You can change it any time. See [Your Ride Name and Profile](/help/ride-name-and-profile).

:::note
On the website, **Continue with Apple** may not be there. Use Apple in the iPhone app, or sign in on the website another way.
:::

## Create an Account With Email and a Password

1. Tap **Create Account** at the top.
2. Enter **Your Name**. This is what riders will see, and you can change it later.
3. Enter your **Email**.
4. Enter a **Password** of at least 8 characters.
5. Tap **Create Account**.
6. If the app says **Almost done**, open the email we sent and tap the link on the same iPhone. Your email is confirmed and you're signed in.

## Sign In With Email and a Password

1. Tap **Sign In** at the top.
2. Enter your **Email** and **Password**.
3. Tap **Sign In**.

## Sign In With an Email Link (No Password)

1. Enter your **Email**.
2. Tap **Or email me a sign-in link instead (no password)**.
3. Open the email on the same iPhone and tap the link.

The link signs you in and opens Home, even if the sign-in screen was still open. If you don't have an account yet, it creates one.

## Reset a Forgotten Password

1. Tap **Sign In** at the top.
2. Enter your **Email**.
3. Tap **Forgot your password? Email me a reset link**.
4. Open the email on your iPhone and tap the link.
5. Enter a **New Password** of at least 8 characters.
6. Tap **Save Password**.

If you see **This Link Has Expired**, tap **Back to Sign In** and ask for a new reset link.

## Opening an Email Link on Another Device

If you tap a link from us in a browser on an iPhone, you may see **Open OnMyLead**. Tap **Open in the App** to finish in the app, or **Continue on the Website** to stay in the browser.

:::release android
On an Android phone or tablet, a link from us opens Chrome for a moment and then OnMyLead, which finishes signing you in. If OnMyLead isn't installed, the website signs you in instead. If you see **Open OnMyLead** in the browser, tap **Open in the App**.
:::

If you see **Your Email Is Confirmed** and a request to sign in again, the link opened somewhere other than where you signed up. Your email is confirmed. Tap **Sign In** and sign in once more with your email and password.

## Sign Out

---

The Starlink page shows how your dish is doing, keeps your plan details in one place, and works out how long your batteries will run it.

## Open the Starlink Page

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **On the Trail**, tap **Starlink**.

## See Your Dish's Live Status

1. Join your Starlink's Wi-Fi network on your iPhone.
2. On the Starlink page, tap **Connect to My Dish**.
3. If your iPhone asks to let OnMyLead find devices on your local network, allow it.

While the page is open, **Your Dish** stays live and shows:

- Whether the dish is online, and its current state.
- **Download Now**, **Upload Now** and **Latency**.
- **Sky Blocked**, **Dropped Pings** and **Up For**.
- Any alerts from the dish.
- The last 15 minutes as a bar chart, with dropouts in red.
- Where the dish is facing, GPS, and its software and hardware versions.

After the first time, the page reconnects by itself when you open it. It stops reading the dish when you leave the page.

:::note
This uses your dish's built-in local connection, which SpaceX doesn't officially support. A Starlink update can break it. Everything else on the page keeps working.
:::

### If It Can't Reach Your Dish

If you see **Can't Reach Your Dish**:

- Make sure your iPhone is on your Starlink Wi-Fi.
- Allow local network access in your iPhone's **Settings**, under **OnMyLead**.

The page keeps trying every 10 seconds. Tap **Retry Now** to try straight away. If it says your dish answered but couldn't be read, a Starlink software update may have changed things. Try again later.

Reading the dish only works in the iPhone app, not on the website.

## Save Your Plan

Starlink doesn't share plan or usage details with other apps, so you can jot them down here. Check your usage in the Starlink app.

1. If you have machines in your [Garage](/help/garage), pick one under **Setup For**, or **General**. Each one keeps its own setup.
2. Under **My Plan**, fill in **Plan**, **Monthly Cost ($)** and **Data Cap (GB)**.
3. Pick your **Dish** and what it's **Powered By**.
4. Add **Notes** like your mount, cable length or router settings.
5. Tap **Save**.

You need to be signed in to save.

## Plan Your Power

Under **Power Budget**:

1. Enter your **Dish Watts**. If you picked your dish, the typical range is shown.
2. Enter **Hours per Day** you'll run it.
3. Under **Battery Size In**, choose **Watt-Hours** or **Amp-Hours + Volts**, then enter your battery size.
4. Set **Usable %**. Use about 90 for lithium and 50 for lead-acid.
5. If you have solar, enter **Solar Watts** and **Sun Hours** per day.

The page shows your **Battery Runtime**, what the **Dish Uses / Day**, what **Solar Adds / Day**, and your daily balance in green or red.

These are estimates. Snow melt, heat and heavy use draw more power. You can use the power calculator without signing in, but you need to sign in to save it.

Ride Mode has big buttons so you can tell the group what's going on without typing. Every rider on the ride sees your tap, and you can see whose phone has it.

![The status buttons in Ride Mode](/help/img/live.webp)

:::warning
Don't use your phone while you're moving. Pull over first, then tap.
:::

## Quick Replies

The four blue buttons send a short message to the group. They also show in the ride chat.

- **On My Way**
- **Running Late**
- **Need a Minute**
- **All Good**

## Status Buttons

The grid below sets your status for the group:

- **OK**
- **Stopped**
- **Need Fuel**
- **Mechanical Issue**
- **Flat Tire**
- **Stuck**
- **Lost**
- **Need Help**
- **EMERGENCY**

**Need Help** sends right away and shows in red for the group. **EMERGENCY** asks you to confirm first. See [Emergencies and Safety](/help/emergency-and-safety).

## Send a Status

1. In Ride Mode, tap a quick reply or a status button.
2. A card appears above the buttons. It says **Sending**, then **Sent to the Group**.
3. Watch the row of lights on the card, one per rider, with their first initial:
   - A solid green light means that rider's app has it.
   - A blue ring means a notification went to their phone, but their app hasn't shown it yet.
   - An empty light means it hasn't reached them yet.

Under the headline, the card spells it out, for example "Seen by Sam and Alex. 2 notified by push." or "All 5 riders got it." Tap **✕** to hide the card. It also goes away on its own after 10 minutes.

## Take It Back

Tapped the wrong button? Tap **Cancel** on the card. The status or quick reply is taken back for everyone, the group is told to ignore it, and the notification they got is replaced with one saying you cancelled it.

## With No Signal

If your tap can't go out within a few seconds, the card says **Is Waiting for Signal**. Your tap is saved on your phone and sends by itself when you get service, stamped with the time you tapped it. Tap **Retry Now** to try again right away, or **Cancel** to drop it.

## Clear Your Status

While your status is anything other than OK, a card on your screen says **Your Status** and what you sent, with a reminder that the group sees it until you mark it resolved. Tap **Resolved, I'm OK** when you're sorted. This sends **OK** to the group.

## Mechanical Issue

**Mechanical Issue** is for a machine that has broken down.

- Your spot shows on the map with an amber wrench, even if you aren't sharing your location. It uses where you were when you tapped.
- The leader, tail gunner and organizers hear it read aloud the moment you tap it, and it stays on their screen until you send another status.
- Your screen shows **Mechanical Issue** with **Fixed, I'm OK**. Tap it once you're rolling again.

**Mechanical Issue** and **EMERGENCY** stay on screen even when you fold the bottom panel away.

## When Another Rider Taps a Status

- A card shows their name, their status and how long ago they tapped it, such as "Sam: Flat Tire, 2 min ago". Tap **Navigate** to get directions to them, or **✕** to hide it on your screen only.
- Calls drop off the list after 30 minutes. A Mechanical Issue stays until that rider sends another status.
- You get a notification on your phone. Need Help and EMERGENCY alerts are always on, even in quiet hours. Other statuses and quick replies follow your **Rider Status** setting. See [Notification Settings](/help/notification-settings).

## Regroup at My Location

Organizers, co-organizers and leaders see a **Regroup at My Location** button above the quick replies. Tap it to set a regroup point where you are.

- Everyone on the ride sees a yellow pin on the map and a yellow banner, **Regroup point set. Tap to navigate**, and hears "Regroup point set."
- Tapping the banner opens directions to the regroup point.
- Setting a new regroup point replaces the old one.

Leaders can also tap **Regroup** on a separation alert. See [Ride Bubble](/help/ride-bubble).

OnMyLead Pro adds unlimited rides, offline maps, GPX import, saved riding groups and more. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro) for the full list.

## Prices

| Plan | US Price |
|---|---|
| **Monthly** | $4.99 a month |
| **Annual** | $29.99 a year, about $2.50 a month. Saves about 50% compared with paying monthly. |

Outside the US, the app shows the price in your local currency.

## Subscribe

1. On the **You** tab, under **Settings**, tap **Subscription**.
2. Tap **Upgrade to Pro**. During your free trial, this button says **Keep Pro After the Trial**.
3. Choose **Annual** (marked **Best Value**) or **Monthly**.
4. Tap the **Subscribe for** button under the plans, for example **Subscribe for $29.99 a Year**.
5. Confirm the purchase in Apple's window.

On Android, step 5 is Google Play's window instead, and the payment goes to your Google Play account.

When it's done, the app says **You’re on OnMyLead Pro. Thanks for riding with us.** and your plan shows **Pro**.

You can also reach the Pro screen by tapping **See OnMyLead Pro** on any Pro prompt, or **Unlimited With Pro** on the Create a Ride screen.

:::note
You can subscribe in the OnMyLead app only, on iPhone, iPad or Android. The website can't sell subscriptions, but Pro you buy in the app also works when you use OnMyLead on the website.
:::

## Already Have Pro From the Other Store?

Pro belongs to your OnMyLead account, so a subscription from the App Store works on Android and one from Google Play works on iPhone and iPad. If you already pay for Pro through one store, the Pro screen on a device that uses the other store says so instead of showing the plans, so you aren't charged twice. To move your subscription to the other store, cancel it in the store you pay now and subscribe on the other device after it ends.

## Billing

- Payment is charged to your Apple Account when you confirm the purchase.
- The subscription renews automatically unless you turn it off at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. Renewal is charged within the 24 hours before the period ends.
- You can manage or cancel anytime in your Apple Account settings. See [Manage or Cancel Your Subscription](/help/manage-subscription).
- On Android, payment is charged to your Google Play account when you confirm. The subscription renews automatically at the end of each period until you cancel it in Google Play, and Pro stays on until the end of the period you paid for.
- The free Pro Trial for new accounts is separate. It needs no payment and never turns into a paid subscription on its own.

The Pro screen links to the **Terms of Use** and **Privacy Policy**.

## If Something Goes Wrong

- **"Waiting on Apple to approve the purchase."** This happens with Ask to Buy or when your bank needs to check the payment. Once it's approved, Pro starts on its own.
- **"Waiting on Google Play to approve the purchase."** This happens when you pay with a method Google confirms later, such as cash at a store. Pro starts on its own once the payment goes through.
- **"The purchase didn’t go through. You weren’t charged."** Check your connection and try again.
- **Your plan still says Free after buying.** Make sure you have signal, then close and reopen the app. If it still says Free, tap **Restore Purchases**. See [Restore Purchases](/help/restore-purchases).

The Trip Planner keeps a packing list for each trip. Tick items off as they go in the rig, and reuse the list next time.

## Open the Trip Planner

1. Go to the **You** tab.
2. Under **Your Gear**, tap **Trip Planner**.

You need to be signed in.

## Plan a New Trip

1. Tap **Plan a New Trip**.
2. Enter a **Trip Name**, like "Moab long weekend".
3. Add dates if you like: **Starts** and **Ends**, written like 2026-10-12. **Ends** is optional.
4. If you have machines in your [Garage](/help/garage), pick the one you're **Taking**.
5. Tap **Create Trip**.

:::note
Free accounts plan one trip at a time. A trip counts until its last day has passed. Planning several trips at once is part of Pro. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).
:::

## Add Items

1. On the trip, tap **Add an Item**.
2. Enter the **Item**, like "Tow strap".
3. Set **How Many** with the number box or the minus and plus buttons.
4. Pick a **Category**, like **Recovery**, **First Aid**, **Camping** or **Food & Water**.
5. Add **Notes** if you like, such as size or where it lives in the rig.
6. Tap **Add**.

Items are grouped by category, each showing how many are packed.

## Start From a Starter List

Tap **Add a Starter List** and pick one, like **Day Ride**, **Overnight / Camping**, **Desert**, **Mountain / Snow**, **Recovery Kit**, **First Aid**, **Tools & Spares** or **Starlink / Power**. One tap adds the items. You can add more than one list, and nothing is added twice.

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Tick Items Off

Tap anywhere on an item's row to check it off. Tap again to uncheck it. The bar at the top shows how much is packed. When everything is checked, it turns green and says so, like All 24 packed.

To change or remove an item, tap **Edit** on its row, then tap **Save** or **Remove Item**.

## After the Trip

Under **After the Trip**:

- **Uncheck All** puts every item back to not packed. The list stays.
- **Copy to a New Trip** starts a new trip with the same list. This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Link a Trip to a Ride

When you create or edit a trip, you can pick a ride you've joined under **For a Ride**. The trip then shows a link to that ride.

This is a Pro feature. See [Free and Pro](/help/free-vs-pro).

## Edit or Delete a Trip

1. Open the trip.
2. Tap **Edit Trip** to change the name, dates, machine or ride, then tap **Save**.
3. Or tap **Delete**, then confirm. The trip and all its items are removed.

## Gear Suggestions

A trip's page may show **Gear From RUS Offroad**, with products that fit your list and machine. See [Gear From RUS Offroad](/help/rus-gear).

---

Start here when something doesn't work the way you expect. If your problem isn't listed, [contact us](/help/contact-support).

## A Rider Shows as a Hollow Dot or "Last Seen"

A rider's dot turns hollow when their last position is more than a minute old, and shows **No Signal** with a dashed grey ring after about 3 minutes. A sharing phone checks in at least every 15 seconds while it has service, so this usually means that rider lost service.

If **everyone** suddenly shows as last seen, it's probably your phone. After about 35 seconds without hearing from the server, Ride Mode shows **No Service. Riders Show Where They Were Last Seen**. It doesn't mark the others as lost because of your own dropout.

See [Share Your Location](/help/location-sharing).

## My Group Can't See Me With My Phone Locked

1. Open your iPhone's **Settings > OnMyLead > Location**.
2. Choose **Always**.
3. Open Ride Mode again. If your share is still running, it picks back up.

On Android, check that the **Sharing Your Location** notification is showing while you share. If it isn't, open Ride Mode again to restart it. If your phone has a battery saver that closes apps, set OnMyLead's battery use to **Unrestricted** in **Settings > Apps > OnMyLead > Battery**.

:::release 1.0.1
If sharing drains your battery too fast on long days, try [Battery Saver](/help/battery-saver). Your group sees you less often, so switch back to **Best Accuracy** when you can charge.
:::

:::release 1.0.1
If Ride Mode shows **Location Is Off**, location is turned off for OnMyLead, so your group can't see you move. Turn it back on in your phone's **Settings**, then open Ride Mode again.
:::

Closing Ride Mode or locking your phone doesn't stop sharing. Sharing ends when your timer runs out, the ride ends, you leave the ride, or you tap **Stop**.

## I Tapped a Status Button With No Signal

It waits on your phone as **Waiting for Signal** and sends by itself as soon as you have service, stamped with the time you tapped it. You can tap **Retry Now** or **Cancel**. See [Status Buttons](/help/status-buttons).

## I'm Not Getting Alerts

1. Check that notifications are allowed for OnMyLead in your iPhone's **Settings > Notifications > OnMyLead**.
2. In the app, open **You** and check your [notification settings](/help/notification-settings), including quiet hours.

On Android, check **Settings > Apps > OnMyLead > Notifications**, including the **Rider Alerts**, **Ride Chat** and **Ride Updates** categories.

**Need Help** and **EMERGENCY** alerts from your group always come through, even in quiet hours, as long as iPhone notifications are allowed for OnMyLead.

## Part of My Route Is a Straight Line

The route builder follows mapped trails. It draws a straight line when no mapped trail joins two points, when the points are very far apart, or when you had no signal and that trail data wasn't saved on your phone. Add a point on the trail or zoom in, or use **Straight Line** for unmapped ground. See [Draw a Route](/help/route-builder).

## I Turned On Trails but See No Lines

Zoom in. Forest Service and BLM lines appear from about zoom level 9 (**Zoom In to See Trails**), and smaller park and local tracks need you to zoom in further (**Zoom In for Park and Local Trails**). The website shows fewer trail layers than the app. See [Map Layers](/help/map-layers).

## My Offline Map Download Stopped

Closing the app pauses a running download. Open **You > Offline Maps** and tap **Resume**, or **Finish** if some pieces are missing. If the area says **Too big for one download**, zoom in so the frame covers less. See [Offline Maps](/help/offline-maps).

## I Don't See a Fuel Check on My Ride

The fuel check needs miles to check against (a saved route or **Route Length (Miles)**) and a machine in your Garage with **Tank (gal)** and **Miles per Gallon** filled in. If you have more than one machine, pick yours under **Bringing** on the ride. See [Fuel Range](/help/fuel-range).

## My Password Reset Link Says It Has Expired

Reset links work once and expire. Tap **Back to Sign In**, ask for a new link, and open it on the same iPhone. See [Sign In](/help/sign-in).

## The Starlink Page Can't Reach My Dish

Your iPhone has to be on the Starlink Wi-Fi, and OnMyLead needs Local Network access (**Settings > OnMyLead**). The page tries again every 10 seconds. It doesn't work on the website. See [Starlink](/help/starlink).

OnMyLead works the same on a tablet as on a phone, with the same account, rides and Pro plan. A tablet just gets layouts made for the bigger screen: the map fills it, and the riders, the ride details and your buttons sit beside the map instead of on top of it.

## Turn It Either Way

Hold the tablet upright or sideways; every screen works both ways. Phones stay upright.

You can also run OnMyLead next to another app (Split View or Slide Over on an iPad, split screen on Android). The layout follows the size of the window: in a narrow window you get the phone layout, and it switches back as the window grows.

## Getting Around

On a tablet, **Rides**, **Find**, **Groups** and **You** run down the left edge of the screen instead of along the bottom.

On **Rides**, with the tablet sideways, **Create a Ride**, **Join a Ride** and **Find a Ride** stay on the left and your rides are listed beside them.

## Ride Mode on a Tablet

The live map fills the screen.

- **Riders** sit in a list on the left with how fresh each rider's location is. Tap the arrow beside a rider to get directions to them. Tap **Hide**, or swipe the list to the left, to see more map; tap **Show Riders** to bring it back. The list starts open with the tablet sideways and folded with it upright.
- **Your buttons** (the route strip, quick replies and status buttons) sit in a panel on the right. Swipe it down or tap **Hide** to fold it, just like on a phone. **Mechanical Issue** and **EMERGENCY** always stay on screen.
- **Directions** and **Add Waypoint** sit just above the buttons panel.
- The ride name, your sharing timer and any announcement stay at the top of the left side.

## The Ride Page

Once you've joined a ride, the ride and its details stay on the left, and **Map**, **Riders** and **Chat** open on the right. You can read the chat or check the route without losing the meeting time and place.

## Draw a Route and Add Waypoints

With the tablet sideways, the route tools and the waypoint list sit in a panel beside the map. Swipe the panel up or tap **Hide** to fold it. With the tablet upright, the panel floats in the bottom corner of the map; swipe it down to fold it.

## Find a Ride

Search and the list of rides sit on the left, with the map filling the rest of the screen.

:::note
Many tablets have no GPS. A Wi-Fi-only tablet can usually only tell roughly where it is, so share your location from your phone on the trail and use the tablet to follow the group.
:::

summary: Mark camp, fuel, water or a hazard on a ride's map, and let the leader plan numbered stops for the whole group.

Waypoints are named spots you drop on a ride's map: camp, fuel, water, a viewpoint, a hazard or parking. Your own waypoints are only for you. The ride's leader can also share waypoints with everyone on the ride, and plan numbered stops the whole group will make.

![Planned stops and waypoints on a ride](/help/img/waypoints.webp)

Waypoints are never public. Shared ones and planned stops show only to riders on that ride.

## Who Sees What

- **Your waypoints**: only you see them, unless you can share (below).
- **Shared waypoints**: the leader or an organizer can share a waypoint with everyone on the ride.
- **Planned stops**: always shared. Every rider sees them numbered on the map, in order.

The leader is the rider with the Leader role, or the organizer when nobody has it. See [Leader, Sweep and Tail Gunner](/help/leader-sweep-and-tail-gunner).

You need to have joined the ride to add or see its waypoints.

## Add a Waypoint

1. Open the ride and tap the **Map** tab.
2. Under **Waypoints**, tap **Add a Waypoint** (or **Open Waypoints Map** if there are some already).
3. Press and hold the map where you want it. To mark where you're standing, tap **Add at My Location** instead.
4. Pick what it is: **Spot**, **Camp**, **Fuel**, **Water**, **Viewpoint**, **Hazard** or **Parking**. The name fills in for you.
5. Change the **Name** if you like, and add a **Note (Optional)**.
6. If you're the leader or an organizer, choose who it's for under **What It Is** (see below).
7. Tap **Save Waypoint**.

In Ride Mode, tap **Add Waypoint** to drop one where you are, or press and hold the map. See [Ride Mode](/help/ride-mode).

Names can be up to 60 characters and notes up to 280.

### Sharing a Waypoint (Leader and Organizers)

When the leader or an organizer adds a waypoint, they choose:

- **Planned Stop**: the whole ride stops here. Numbered on every rider's map.
- **Everyone on the Ride**: shows on every rider's map.
- **Just Me**: only you see it.

New waypoints from the leader or an organizer start as **Everyone on the Ride**, and you can switch to **Just Me**.

## Plan the Ride's Stops

Planned stops tell everyone where the group will stop for fuel, lunch or camp, and in what order.

1. Open the ride and tap the **Map** tab.
2. Under **Planned Stops**, tap **Add a Planned Stop**.
3. Press and hold the map where the group will stop.
4. Pick what it is and give it a name.
5. Add a **Planned Time (Optional)**, like "12:30 pm".
6. Tap **Save Planned Stop**.

Stops are numbered in the order you add them. To change the order:

1. Tap a planned stop on the map or in the list.
2. Tap **Move Earlier** or **Move Later**.

The leader or an organizer can edit any planned stop on the ride, even ones someone else added, so the plan carries on if the leader changes.

## View, Navigate, Edit or Remove

Tap a waypoint on the map or in the list to open it. You'll see its type, who it's from, the note and its coordinates.

- **Navigate**: get directions in your maps app. See [Directions](/help/directions).
- **Edit**: change it. You can edit your own waypoints. The leader or an organizer can also edit planned stops.
- **Remove**: take it off the map. You can remove your own. The leader or an organizer can also remove shared ones. When a shared waypoint is removed, everyone stops seeing it.

## On the Website

The waypoints map works on onmylead.com too. Click the map to drop a waypoint, and click a waypoint to open it.

On a tablet held sideways, the waypoint list sits beside the map; swipe it up or tap **Hide** to fold it.

## No Signal

The waypoints you can see are saved on your phone, so they stay on the map without signal. The panel shows **Saved on This Phone** when that's what you're seeing.

## Limits

Each rider can add up to 100 waypoints on a ride. If you reach that, remove one to add another.

:::note
Waypoints are different from the numbered points you tap when drawing a route. Route points shape the line; waypoints mark places along the way.
:::
